full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: A Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order contained in Memo No. 1767 dated 22-1-97 (Annexure-J) passed by the respondent No 1 in Abdul Gani Waqf Estate bearing EC No 2059 (Chittagong) staying the eviction order passed by him on 1-9-96 should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

<u>2. The petitioner, Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate in his application under Article 102 of the Constitution stated, inter alia, that his predecessor dedicated the property in Waqf Free Sabilillah by registered Waqf Deed No. 1402 dated 23-2-1928 and appointed himself as the first Mutwalli in respect of property being Mouza-Sholoshahar, Police Station Panchlaish, CS Plot No.3318 (4 and half Ganda from western side) CS plots No. 3348, 3360 area of 10 Ganda, CS Plot No 4276/3361, CS Plot No. 3329/3330/3331 area of 9 and half Ganda, CS Plot No 3335/3336 area of 8 Ganda, CS Plot No 3357 area one Kani, CS Plot No 3295 area of 5 Ganda and of Mouza-Bakalia, CS Plot Nos. 311/314/315/316/317/318/320/321/322/323/324/325/326/336/337/338/339/340/341/342/343/344/345/346/347/348/350/351/353/354/ area 6 Kani 13 Ganda 2 Kara and the total land being 12 Kani 13 Ganda 2 Kara. The said Waqf Estate was duly enrolled with the Office of Administrator of Waqf Dhaka being EC No 2059 (Chittagong) as Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. Upon appointment of Mutwalli the petitioner found that 2.67 acres of Waqf properties has been forcibly and illegally occupied by the trespassers whereupon the petitioner filed an application on 27-1-96 before the Administrator of Waqf, for an order initiating proceedng under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 for recovery of the possession of the Waqf Estate from illegal and unauthorized trespassers. The latter by order contained in memo No.1302/Chatta dated 15-4-1996 directed the petitioner to file an application under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. Whereupon the Waigif Administrator of Dhaka by his order contained in Memo No 267/Chatta dated 1-9-1996 ordered the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to evict the unauthorized occupiers and possessors from the Waqf land.</u>

<u>3. Pursuant to said order the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong by order contained in Memo No. 362/1(6)/RM dated 28-10-1996 appointed Mr Helal Mahmud Sharif, the Assistant Commissioner, Chittagong to execute eviction proceeding and hand over the vacant possession to the petitioner who in his turn by letter in Memo 1536(B)/1/JM dated 3-12-1996 directed the Deputy Police Commissioner (North) Chittagong Metropolitan Police, Sadar, to arrange necessary police force on 30-12-1996 for executing the eviction proceeding. The said date of execution of the eviction proceeding was refaxed on 9-1-97 on which day some illegal trespassers from the land covered under BS Khatian No. 2908, BS Plot Nos 139/140/141 were evicted and possession was handed over of the same to the Petitioners-Mutwalli and submitted his report under Memo, No 81(8)JM dated 19-1-97. On 20-1-97 Manjur Ahmed the respondent No. 2 filed an application before the Administrator of Waqf, Dhaka under'' section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance claiming property in BS Khatian No 2937 BS Plot No.124 /12 5/126/1141/1142/1143/1145/1261/1262/ 23603 /23604 of Mouza-Bakalia stating that the said property has nothing to do with the property of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate bearing EC No.2059 (Chittagong) and prayed for withdrawal of the eviction order. The said application was registered as Waqf Miscellaneous Case No 29 of 1996 and Administrator of Waqf respondent No.1 by the impugned order dated 22-1-97 stayed the eviction proceeding pending final decision and for maintaining status quo.</u>

4. The respondent No 2 contested the Rule filing Affidavit-in-Opposition stating, inter alia, that the schedule of the petitioner Waqf Estate as stated in the application by the petitioner for eviction is not true and correct. The lands of schedule-2 of the petition being plot No 311, 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 320, 321, 322, 323, 324, 325, 326, 336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341, 342, 343, 344, 345, 346, 347, 348, 350, 351, 353, 354 are not the property of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. These are the property of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate created on 5-10-28 being the subject matter of EC No 1690 of which the respondent and his two brothers are joint Mutwallis. The petitioner suppressed the same without impleading the respondent in the application have illegally sought to evict the respondent No 2 from the said plots which are recorded In the name of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate in RS and BS operation. The present BS Plots in respect of those RS Plots also recorded in the name of respondent and his brother Mutwalli. Some of the property stood in their personal names and all the plots are in their possession. The respondent further asserted that the land appertaining to BS Khatian No.2935, 683, 2937, 2938 belong to the respondent and their Waqf Estate in the Khatian standing in their names. The respondent has further denied that 2.67 acres of land of EC No. 2059 or any other land has been forcibly possessed by trespassers. The petitioner''s claim in the petition under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance is not true but a misrepresentation of fact for obtaining illegal possession under the Waqf Ordinance. On 9-1-97 the respondent could learn about the illegal proceeding when all on a sudden the Magistrate went on the land belonging to the respondent Waqf Estate. The impugned action of eviction of alleged trespassers having been conducted behind the back of respondent No. 2 designed to illegally take over possession of land belonging to the respondent No. 2''s Waqf Property under the garb of section 64(1) of the Ordinance, was done without notifying persons concerned and without determining as to whether the land actually belongs to the petitioner's said Waqf Estate or whether the occupiers are trespassers or not. The respondent has further submitted that the said ex parte order of eviction of alleged trespassers without ascertaining and determining as to whether the land belongs to Waqf Estate of the petitioner or whether the occupiers are trespassers thereto, the order of eviction was wholly without jurisdiction and the Waqf Administrator did not commit any illegality or has not acted without jurisdiction in staying further proceeding of the eviction pending decision on the application under 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance. During the pendency of the Rule an application for addition of party as respondent No. 3 on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong was filed and moved and this Court by order dated 27-5-97 directed that the application be kept on record to be disposed of at the time of hearing of the Rule. However the said application was not pressed at the time of hearing and accordingly, the said application is rejected as not pressed.

5. Mr Momtazuddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing with Mr Sk Julfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, Advocate for the petitioner has submitted that the Waqf Administrator acted illegally and without lawful authority in staying the further proceeding of eviction order in a proceeding initiated under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance contained in his Memo No. 267/Chittagong debated 1-9-96 having been focus officio inasmuch as after passing the final order dated 1-9-96 for eviction of the trespassers the respondent No. 1 could not entertain an application dated 20-1-97 filed by the respondent No. 2 under section 64(1) of the said Waqf Ordinance. The learned DAG has further submitted that the respondent could however prefer an appeal against the said order of eviction under section 64(2) of the Ordinance, instead illegally resorted to a fresh application under section 64(1) upon which the impugned order was passed illegally staying his eviction proceeding.

6. Mr M A Jalil, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 2 has submitted that the Waqf Administrator acted lawfully and with jurisdiction in passing an order of stay pending decision on the application under section 64(1) of the Ordinance filed by the respondent No. 2 pending enquiry and decision on the allegation therein that the order of eviction has been made in respect of the land of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate being numbered EC No. 1690. The learned Advocate further submits that alleged order of eviction was passed behind the back of respondent No. 2 and the Mutwalli's of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate to which the lands in dispute belong are entitled to apply to the Waqf Administrator for enquiry and ascertain the land in question allegedly trespassed and as such, no question of preferring an appeal arises in the facts of the present case inasmuch as no formal order having been passed by the Waqf Administrator under section 64(1) upon the application of the petitioner, the question of restoring the appeal under sub-section 2 of section 64 of the Ordinance is not warranted.

7. Mr Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 1 though has not filed any Affidavit-in-Opposition on behalf of the said respondent, has however adopted the submissions made on behalf of the respondent No. 2.

8. It appears from Annexure-C, a copy of the application under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 wherein the petitioner has stated that few days back he has been appointed as a Mutwalli and the land mentioned in the schedule thereto are in illegal possession of the persons namely, Manjur Ahmed (respondent No 2), Abu Taher and Nasir Uddin, sons of Munshi Azizur Rahman of West Bakalia, DC Road, PS Chandgaon, Chittagong and the petitioner tried to recover possession but said persons denying the right of Waqf Estate in schedule land have constructed many houses and the said illegal acts were done due to the callousness of the previous Mutwalli and if the trespassers are evicted, the income of the Waqf Estate will be enhanced to a great extent. The schedule of land mentioned the lands of CS Plots No 311/314/316/317/318/320/321/322/323/324/325/326/336/337/338/339/340/341/342/343/344/345/346/347/348/350/351/353/354 with an area of 6 kani 13 Ganda 2 Kara and the houses standing on some of these plots. On receipt of the said application on 17-5-96 the Waqf Administrator by his Memo No 268/Chittagong dated 1-9-96 addressed the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong requesting to take necessary action under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 in respect of the mentioned Waqf Estate (Annexure-D). It further appears from Annexure-E a letter issued by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong addressed to Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate of the office of Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong contained in Memo No 362/1/(6)/RM dated 28-10-96 directing him to evict the illegal trespassers from the schedule land mentioned therein and to hand over possession to the petitioner giving the schedule described as BS Khatian No.2935, BS Dag No.195, 196,93,94.95, 113, 114, 122, 123, 129, 130, 136,138, 142, 113/322 BS Khatian No 683, 13S Dag No 111, 129, 130 139, 136, 137, 138, 142, 113/323'' B S Khatian No. 2938, B/S Dag No.127, 128, 139, 145, 141, BS Khatian No. 882 BS Dag No.21, BS Rhatian No.3234, BS Dag No 17, BS Khatian No. 722 BS Dag No 17 BS Khatian No 3345, BS Dag No 19.20, 16/321 BS Khatian Khatian No 1620, BS Dag No. 18. Neither the said Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate nor the Waqf Administrator nor the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) or the Additional Deputy Commissioner issued any notice upon the alleged trespassers including the respondent No 2 to ascertain the fact of trespass and illegal construction on their part in the disputed lands by the alleged trespassers and themselves also did not ascertain as to whether the lands belong to the said Waqf Estate or that the occupiers are trespassers therein or not. But it appears from Annexure-H being Memo No. 81(4)/JM dated 19-1-97 of the Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong allegedly stating that by holding eviction proceeding in part he has handed over possession of plot No.139, 140 and 141 of BS Khatian No 2938 to the petitioner, Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. There are good numbers of timber shop, saloons, Pharmacy, Grocers shop and restaurants and the shop owners on the said plot have executed stamps of Taka 50.(X) (fifty) admitting that they are the tenants under the Waqf Estate.

<u>9. Thereafter the respondent No 2 filed an application in the said proceeding in Waqf Misc. Case No.29 of 1996 on 20-1-97 to the Waqf Administrator under section 64(1) claiming the disputed land in question belonging to the Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate being EC No 1690 and not to Abdul Gani Waqf Estate RC No 2059 and that no notice was ever served upon the alleged trespassers including the respondent No 2 and thus procured the ex parte order of eviction and caused the alleged eviction commenced on 9-1-97 when the respondent No 2 learnt about the same and an enquiry and hearing are absolutely necessary in the matter for consideration of the relevant papers and documents of the respective parties and as such prayed, inter alia, for stay of the eviction process Vide Memo No. 267/Chatta, dated 1-9-96 directing the Deputy Commissioner to withdraw his order. Upon the said application the Waqf Administrator respondent No. 1 passed the impugned order directing status quo pending disposal of the application upon hearing the parties and accordingly stayed the further proceeding for eviction fixing 16-2-97 for hearing. Thereafter the petitioner has moved this Court and obtained the present Rule and stay.</u>

10. It has been submitted, on our query, by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that in spite of the stay order passed by this Court no further action in the matter of eviction was conducted, instead the Deputy Commissioner himself wanted to be a party to the Rule by an application moved in this Court on 27-5-97, disposed of earlier in this judgment. In the said application on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner for impleading as respondent No 3 it has been stated that the Administrator of Waqf upon an application under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance for recovery of the possession of the Waqf land from illegal and unauthorized trespassers and on proper scrutiny the Administrator of Waqf by his order under Memo No 267/Chatta dated 1-9-96 ordered the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to evict the unauthorized occupiers and possessors from the Waqf land bearing EC No 2059 (Chittagong) and in view of the order dated 1-9-96, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong by order dated 28-10-96 appointed Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate to execute eviction proceeding and hand over the vacant possession to the petitioner and consequently Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate by his letter under Memo No 1536(8)1/JM dated 3-12-96 requested the Deputy Police Commissioner (W) Chittagong Metropolitan Police, Sadar to arrange necessary police force for evicting the trespassers and on 9-1-97 unauthorized occupiers and possessors were evicted from land covered under BS Khatian No. 2908 BS Plot No. 139/140/141 and handed over possession to the petitioner. It appears from the schedule to the waqf deed (Annexure-A) that the waqf land have been described with reference to CS Plots as aforesaid, similarly, the petitioner in his application Annexure ''C'' under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance described the Waqf land with reference to said CS Plots of Mouza-Bakalia Police Station Panchalaish, District-Chittagong without mentioning the CS Khatian thereof with areaf of 6 Kani 13 Ganda 2 Kara with houses and buildings standing on part thereof and it would appear from Annexure-D dated 1-9-96 that the respondent No.1 has referred the said application dated 12-5-96 for necessary action to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong but it appears from the Annexure-E, that on 28-10-96 Additional Deputy Commissioner directed the Assistant Commissioner/and Magistrate to make over possession of certain lands described with reference to CS Khatian and BS Plots by evicting the unauthorized occupants to the Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. It further appears from Annexure-F that said Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate, Sadar fixed 30-12-96 for making over delivery of possession to the said Mutwalli by evicting the unauthorized occupiers from the waqf land described with reference to certain BS Khatians and BS Plots without any specification and boundary thereof. The quantum of land has not been stated therein and from Annexure-H, the report of that Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate it appears that eviction of alleged trespassers have been carried out from some part of the disputed land particularly from plots Nos.139, 149, 141 of BS Khatian No.2398 and handed over alleged possession to the Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate.

<u>11. Section 36 of the Waqf Ordinance provides exercise of powers through Deputy Commissioner as under:</u>

<u>"Subject to any rules made in this behalf, the Administrator may exercise any of the powers conferred on him by this Ordinance through the Deputy Commissioner of the district in which the waqf property concerned is situated or through any other person whom he may appoint for such purpose and may, from time to time, delegate any of his powers to such Deputy Commissioners or other persons as aforesaid and may, at any time, revoke such delegation."</u>

<u>Rule 12 of the Waqf Administrator Rules, 1975 has been framed to carry out the purpose under section 36 and the relevant rules are quoted as under:</u>

<u>"Rule 12(1). In special cases, the Administrator may delegate the following powers under section 36 of the Ordinance to any Deputy Commissioner of a District:</u>

<u>(a) General power and functions of the Administrator under clause (a) of section 27 of the Ordinance</u>

<u>(II) The Administrator may require the Deputy Commissioner of a district to have an inspection of any waqfs enrolled in the Waqfs Register of that district either by himself or any officer subordinate to him. He may also authorise with regard to the administration of such waqfs or any complaint against the mutawalli of such waqfs or any other matter relating to such waqfs and the Deputy Commissioner can make the inquiry himself or through an officer subordinate to him."</u>

<u>Section 27 of the Waqf Ordinance:</u>

<u>Subject to the provisions of this Ordinance and the rule made the under the powers and functions of the Administrator shall include.</u>

<u>(a) Investigating and determining the nature and extent of Waqf and Waqf properties and calling from time to time, for accounts, returns and information from Mutwallis.</u>

<u>12. The said section 36 of the Waqf Ordinance provides that Waqf Administrator may exercise any of the powers conferred on him by the Ordinance through the Deputy Commissioner of the District in which the Waqf property concerned is situated or through any other persons he may appoint for such purpose from time to time and delegate any of his powers to such Deputy Commissioner or other persons and at any time, remove, such delegation. On perusal of aforesaid rule 12(1)(a) it appears that delegation of the powers of Administrator of Waqf to the Deputy Commissioner of a district may be for general power and function of the Administrator under clause (a) of section 27 of the Ordinance. Section 27 of the Ordinance provides the power and function of the administrator which include investigating and determining the nature and extent of the Waqf and Waqf property. Under Rule 12(11) the Administrator may require the Deputy Commissioner to have an inspection of properties of any enrolled waqf by himself through any officer subordinate to him and the Administrator may also authorize the Deputy Commissioner to make inquiries with regard to Waqf or any other matter relating to such waqf and the Deputy Commissioner can make the inquiry himself or through an officer subordinate to him.</u>

13. It is clear from Annexure-D dated 1-9-96 that on receipt of the application under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance dated 12-5-96 the Administrator of Waqf did neither hold any investigation nor determine or inquire as to the alleged trespass but referred the matter to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong for necessary action.

<u>14. Section 36 of the Ordinance authorizes the Administrator to delegate his power to the Deputy Commissioner for the purpose of investigating and determining the nature and extent of Waqf and Waqf properties and the Administrator may also require the Deputy Commissioner to have an inspection of properties of a Waqf enrolled or make enquiries with regard to any matter relating to such waqf and the Deputy Commissioner can make such inquiry himself or through an officer subordinate to him. Thus section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance provides that if a co-sharer in waqf property or an individual beneficiary or any other person interested in a Waqf or a stranger, created disturbance or obstruction in the peaceful management of waqf or disturbed the possession'' of a Waqf Property by the MutWalli or committed trespass on any such property, the Administrator shall apply to the Deputy Commissioner who shall evict the trespassers or take such steps for preventing such disturbance or obstruction as he may deem fit. So under section 64(1) the Administrator of Waqf has been empowered to direct the Deputy Commissioner to evict the trespassers or take such step for preventing such disturbance or obstruction as he may deem fit. According to said section, in our view, while evicting the trespassers, a duty is cast upon the Administrator to ascertain the trespass, the person involved therein and the disputed land in question which has been trespassed. This he could do himself under section 27 by investigating and determining the nature and extent of waqf and waqfs properties and the persons involved in the said waqf property committing trespass. He can, however, delegate his power to the Deputy Commissioner of the District for investigating and determining the nature and extent of waqf and waqfs properties by way of an inspection or inquiry into any other matter relating to the waqf to be made by Deputy Commissioner by himself or through an official subordinate to him. In the instant facts and circumstances as detailed above, upon receipt of application of the petitioner dated 12-5-97 the Waqf Administrator without investigating and determining the extent and nature of waqf and waqf properties and without ascertaining the trespass, the persons involved and the disputed land in question as to the alleged trespass was into a good number of CS Plots of Mouza-Bakalia, PS Chandgaon and without ascertaining by way of enquiry and investigation and inspection either by himself and  through the Deputy Commissioner or official subordinate to him has referred the application to the. Deputy Commissioner for necessary action by his Memo dated 1-9-95 and without any order of Deputy Commissioner, the Additional Deputy Commission and the Commissioner and Magistrate have caused eviction of alleged trespassers from certain BS Plots under BS Khatian. The waqf deed and the application dated 12-5-97 described the waqf land in terms of CS Plots but meanwhile two more surveys named RS and BS have occurred. Admittedly no survey or repayment has been made as to the CS Plots appearing in the Waqf deed and the application dated 12-5-97 with BS Plots of BS Khatians, suddenly appearing in the Memo of Additional Deputy Commissioner and Magistrate for the first time in order to carry out the eviction of the alleged trespassers from the land and building standing on the good numbers of BS Plots without any demarcation and/or specification as to boundary. It is very clear from the Memo dated 1-9-96 issued by the Waqf Administrator in favour of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong that there was absolutely no order for eviction of the alleged trespasser but was directed to take necessary action under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance. But the Deputy Commissioner without determining or investigating into the matter as required under the law mechanically directed Additional Deputy Commissioner to effect eviction as stated above. Moreover, there is neither any enquiry nor any inspection or any investigation and determination as to the nature and extent of the waqf and waqf property for evicting the alleged trespassers on the disputed land in question which has been trespassed. The process of eviction as has been done, have no sanction of law. The impugned order goes to show that the Waqf Administrator has passed the order of ''status quo'' and stayed the further proceeding of order of eviction till the matter is finally decided by the Waqf Administrator. Under section 21 of the General Clauses Act the authority, the Waqf Administrator could as well stay the order of eviction directing status quo and stay of further proceeding of eviction process even if assuming that by his Memo dated 1-9-96 the Waqf Administrator has ordered the Deputy Commissioner to carry out the eviction of the trespassers pending disposal of the said application.</u>

15. Thus from the above discussion it is clear that the Waqf Administrator is empowered under law to direct an order of status quo and staying further proceeding of alleged eviction proceeding pending hearing of the application of the respondent No. 2 in accordance with law and such order was also warranted for ends of justice in the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the rival claim of the respondent No 2 in respect of the selfsame land to be the subject matter of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate and also to determine the disputed property to be the Waqf property of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate or not.

<u>16. In view of the above legal position we are of the view that no appeal as contemplated under sub-section 64(2) is required to be availed of by the respondent No.2 as the respondent No 1 has passed the impugned order pending disposal of the application of the respondent No 2 claiming the disputed land to be the subject matter of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate (RC No 1690).</u>

Accordingly, we do not find any substance in the submission of learned Deputy Attorney-General. The Rule is accordingly discharged but without any order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
Ozair Farooq with SK Md Morshed, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
M Amir-ul Islam with Md Rafiqul Islam—For Respondent Nos. 4 & 5.

parties:
SM Delwar Hossain and others ----- Petitioners 
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
SAN Mominur Rahman J: The Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Office Order No. 1146 dated 25-2-2007 circulated under Memo No. 1146/1(8) dated 25-2-2007, issued under the signature of the respondent No. 3, constituting an Ad-hoc Managing Committee superseding the existing elected Managing Committee of Bohumukhi Khudra Kutir Shilpa Samabava Samity Ltd, evidenced by Annexure-D to the writ petition, should not be declared t be without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

2. The Rule is opposed by filing affidavit-in-opposition by the added respondent Nos. 4 and 5. The petitioners filed affidavit-in-reply there against.

3. The writ petitioners are the elected Members and Office Bearers of the Bohumukhi Khudra Kutir Shilpa Samabaya Samity Ltd, hereinafter referred to as the Samity. The petitioner No. 1 SM Delwar Hossain is the President of the Managing Committee, The election was held on 31-7-05.

4. The Samity started functioning with 12 Members Management Committee, whose term expired on 6-3-1998 and under the said committee, a new Managing Committee of the Samity was elected on 6-8-1998 (should be 6-3-1998) for a period of three years, whose tenure expired on 6-3-2001 and that the said elected Managing Committee could not hold the election for electing the next Managing Committee as per Constitution, because of dispute amongst the members. Consequently an Ad-hoc Managing Committee with three persons, was formed for a period of 90 days for holding election of Management Committee by the authority vide Memo dated 11-3-2001 and the tenure of the said Ad-hoc Committee was extended up to 30-9-2001. Thereafter, the authority appointed another Ad-hoc Committee consisting of seven persons vide Memo dated 22-10-2001 for holding election of Managing Committee within 31-1-2002. The said Committee also could not hold the election of the Managing Committee and another Cronkite was formed for holding election vide Memo dated 28-4-2002 and the said Managing Committee published the voters list on 16-5-2003 fixing the election date on 28-5-2003, but one Md Shamsul Islam by filing Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 obtained a Rule and restraint order as to the voter list, for which the election could not be held. Subsequently on 11-5-05, the said Rule was discharged for default and the restraint order was vacated and in the meantime, Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 was filed by Md. Delwar Hossain and another, challenging the formation of the Ad-hoc Committee by the authority vide Order No. 3506 dated 26-9-04 and there was no order of stay passed in the said writ petition. The tenure of the Ad-hoc Committee appointed vide said Memo dated 26-9-2004 expired on 25-12-2004 and then the Government upon exercising its power under section 4 of the Co-operative Societies Act, 2001, hereafter referred to as the Societies Act, exempted the Sanity from the operation of section 18(5)(7) of the Societies Act and extended the tenure of the said Ad-hoc Managing Committee for one year more and that the Rule issued in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 was made absolute vide judgment and order dated 27-6-2005 declaring the managing committee as illegal and without lawful authority and the Registrar, Co-operative Societies, was directed to form a fresh Ad-hoc Managing Committee with Government officials for holding election in one month and subsequently by filing CPLA No. 444 of 2005 against the aforesaid judgment and order dated 27-6-2005 an order of stay was obtained from the Appellate Division and thereafter the CPLA No. 937 of 2005 was filed in due course and the period of stay was extended and that upon the discharge of the Rule and the order of restraint being vacated in Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 and in view of granting of the stay order by the Appellate Division staying operation of the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, as mentioned hereinabove, the Ad-hoc Managing Committee, under challenge, by a notice dated 16-6-2005 convened a Special General Meeting of the Samity on 21-8-2005 for holding election of the Managing Committee of the Samity and that the Secretary of the Managing Committee by letter dated 12-7-2005 sought approval of three-member Election Committee from the District Co-operative Officer, Dhaka, who by his order dated 12-7-2005, approved the same, and the said Election Committee declared the election schedule on 14-7-2005 fixing voting date on 31-7-2005 and accordingly, published the voters list and that only 12 candidates having submitted nomination papers against 12 posts, no formal election was held on 31-7-2005 and the said 12 candidates were declared elected uncontested in the respective posts and the said result was circulated to all concerned and thereafter the Special General Meeting of the Samity was held on 21-8-2005 pursuant to the notice dated 16-6-2005, and in the said meeting the election result was officially declared and the newly elected Managing Committee of the Samity entered into office and have been functioning, which fact was informed to the District Co-operative Officer, Dhaka, by the Samity vide Memo dated 23-8-2005 and the said new Managing Committee held an Annual General Meeting of the Samity on 15-9-2005, wherein 233 general members were present and several decisions were taken for the development of the Samity. The Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 was subsequently restored on 31-8-2005 subject to holding of election, since in the meantime an election has been held on 31-7-05. Subsequently, one Md Shamsul Islam filed Writ Petition No. 8721 of 2005 challenging the election result dated 31-7-2005, so far relates to the office of the President, wherein the Rule was issued on 4-12-2005 and a direction was also issued to the effect that the nature and structure of the market place of the Samity should not be changed and that the said Writ Petition No. 8721 of 2005 and Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 were heard one after another and disposed of by a single judgment and order dated 23-8-2006, discharging both the Rules together with the interim orders, and that the writ petitioner of the Writ Petition No. 8721 of 2005 moved the Appellate Division unsuccessfully with Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 892 of 2006 with a prayer for stay of operation of the judgment and order dated 23-8-06 passed in Writ Petition No. 8721 of 2005; and that the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 937 of 2005, arising out of the Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, was dismissed, since became in fructuous, on 15-2-2007.

5. The learned Advocate for the writ petitioner hereof submitted that the Leave Petition No. 937 of 2005 was dismissed on consideration that in the meantime the election of the Managing Committee was held on 31-7-2005; and that misinterpreting the order passed by the Appellate Division dated 15-2-2007 dismissing the leave petition and without considering the fact that the dismissal order was passed since the petition became infructuous because of the election held on 31-7-2005, the District Co-operative Officer, Dhaka, constituted an Ad-hoc Managing Committee superseding the elected Managing Committee of the Samity, purportedly in compliance to the judgment and order passed in the Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, and the said constitution of the Ad-hoc Managing Committee is under challenge in the instant Rule.

6. The respondent Nos. 4 and 5 in their affidavit-in-opposition asserted that the Ad-hoc Managing Committee of 2002 intentionally included the same persons in the voters list in violation of the mandatory provisions of the Samity's Constitution and the voters list published on 16-5-2002 included the voters in serial Nos. 552 to 634 of the said voters list, not qualified to become members, for which the Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 was filed, wherein Rule and restraint order was passed on 22-5-2002 and no election could be held with the said voters list and that in collusion to each other, i.e., the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 and of Civil Petition No. 937 of 2005, held the election dated 31-7-2005 allowing discharge of the Rule for default in Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 and thereafter the Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 was restored on 31-8-2005 and that the said election dated 31-7-2005 was held to frustrate the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 and that the High Court Division in the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 made the Rule absolute declaring the Managing Committee as illegal and without lawful authority and directing the Registrar, Co-operative Societies, for formation of a fresh Ad-hoc Managing Committee by the Government officials for holding the election within one month from the date of receipt of the judgment and order and that after the dismissal of the Civil Petition No. 937 of 2005, the Ad-hoc Committee was formed accordingly, which has been challenged in the instant writ petition. The 12 member Committee formed on 26-9-2004, which held the election on 31-7-05, has been declared to be illegal and without lawful authority and the said committee resorting to fraud held the said election to frustrate the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004. After the disposal of the Civil Petition No. 937 of 2005 the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 revived and came into force and accordingly, the legality of the constitution of the five member Ad-hoc Managing Committee of the Samity, pursuant to the judgment and order dated 27-6-2005 passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, cannot be called into question and that the said five-member Ad-hoc Committee having been made pursuant to the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the question of issuance of any show cause notice, as claimed, does not arise.

7. In the affidavit-in-reply, the facts stated in the writ petition have been asserted and the statements made in the affidavit-in-opposition have been denied.

8. On perusal of the writ petition and on hearing the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties, it appears to us that the moot question for resolution is that whether the five-member Ad-hoc Committee formed in compliance to the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, with Writ Petition No. 8721 of 2005, is in accordance with law or not and is in force, on the ground that in the meantime an election was held on 31-7-2005 taking advantage of the stay order from the Appellate Division in CPLA No. 937 of 2005 and the order of discharge of the Rule in Writ Petition No. 2520 of 2002 for default.

9. Mr Md Ozair Farooq, the learned Advocate appearing for the writ petitioners, submits that the election dated 31-7-2005 was held in accordance with law and has been approved by the Appellate Division while dismissing the CPLA No. 937 of 2005, ordering that the same has become in fructuous inasmuch as the operation of the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 was stayed in said CPLA No. 937 of 2005 and thus the Appellate Division taking cognizance of the election held on 31-7-2005 found that the continuation of the Civil Petition No. 937 of 2005 will be of no effect and since the litigations were for holding an election of a Managing Committee of the Samity and that the election has already been held with the Members of the Samity without any objection on 31-7-2005 and that the said elected Committee entered into the office and has been functioning in normal course, which also held the Annual General Meeting of the Samity; and that a writ petition was filed challenging the election of 31-7-2005 being Writ Petition No. 8721 of 2005 and the Rule issued in the said writ petition was subsequently discharged, against which the writ petitioner thereof unsuccessfully moved the Appellate Division and thereby the election dated 31-7-2005 continued to function within the knowledge of the Appellate Division. The learned Advocate then submits that since the election of 31-7-2005 has not been disturbed by the Appellate Division, the formation of the impugned Ad-hoc Committed by the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Society for holding fresh election is redundant and against law.

10. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 submitted that the judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, was in existence, when the so-called election was held on 31-7-05, but the operation of the said judgment and order was stayed, at the instance of the persons, who were Members of the Managing Committee declared to be illegal, by the High Court Division. The learned Advocate submitted that Md Delwar Hossain, the Chairman of the present Managing Committee, is behind all these things and writ petitioner No. 1 of Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 is instrumental in holding the election dated 31-7-2005. The learned Advocate submitted that the members of the present Managing Committee, this way or that way, are holding the office of the Management Committee, since its inception and are not allowing holding of any free and fair election. The learned Advocate submits that since the writ petitioner hereof is aware about the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, wherein the existing Management Committee was declared to be illegal and without lawful authority, and the members of the said Management Committee declared illegal in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, having held the election of 31-7-2005 and the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, not being set aside, or annulled, with the dismissal of the CPLA. No. 937 of 2005, revived and came into force, and the said judgment of the High Court Division cannot be allowed to be frustrated by any process and that the impugned Committee having been formed in compliance to the said judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, the election of 31-7-05 held by the Committee, which was declared illegal and without lawful authority by the High Court Division, as aforementioned, is of no legal effect and has no validity in the eye of law and therefore the said election is a nullity in the eye of law.

<u>11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and having regard to the fact that the CPLA No. 937 of 2005 was dismissed and thereby the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 revived and remained unaltered and is in force and therefore the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004 is binding on the parties. In the instant case, it appears that the election of 31-7-2005 was conducted at the instance of the Committee, which was declared to be illegal and without lawful authority by the judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004, and the said writ petition being mainly for holding of free and fair election of a Managing Committee of the Samity, the election as held by the said illegal Committee on 31-7-2005 cannot be said to be bonfire and the election conducted by an illegal authority cannot sustain in the eye of law. Thus we find substance in the submission made by the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and we do not find any merit in the Rule.</u>

<u>12. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost.</u>

<u>The election held on 31-7-2005 is declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and not valid in the eye of law and impugned Committee as formed, and under challenge in this Rule, is declared to be in accordance with law and the said five-member Committee is directed to hold the election within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order and the Committee, if necessary, be reconstituted with available government officials. The day-to-day activities as performed and the expenses made by the Management Committee elected on 31-7-05 will be valid subject to approval in the Annual General Meeting to be convened and held by the new elected Managing Committee, to be elected as per direction of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 5807 of 2004.</u>

End.

parties:
Eklas Miah (Md)  ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Monohor Ali and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md. Awlad Ali, J: This revisional application by the defendants under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure arises out of the judgment and order dated 28-2-93 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Temporary Court, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1992 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. Facts leading to the application is that, one Md Azfar Ali predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 1-5 instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 409 of 1976 in the First Court of Sadar Munsif at Sylhet praying for partition of certain ejmali lands on declaration of their title. In the said suit the opposite parties in the instant application and others were impleaded as defendants. The suit was decreed on contest in preliminary form on 9-1-91. Thereafter the preliminary decree was made final on 2-4-1984. The petitioners thereafter filed Title Execution Case No. 21 of 1985 praying for delivery of possession of their saham. While the proceeding of execution case was pending the present opposite parties as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 301 of 1986 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 114 of 1990 after it was transferred to the Additional Assistant Judge, Sylhet, praying for setting aside the decree on the ground of fraud. In the suit plaintiff also made an application under Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for stay of further proceeding of the above execution case but that application was rejected on 30-9-86. The plaintiff opposite party then moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 176 of 1986 and the Rule was made absolute on 26-8-87 and the matter was sent back to the learned Assistant Judge concerned for fresh hearing and disposal of the said application. While disposing of the revisional application this court ordered that the application filed on 30-9-86 praying for stay by the petitioner be disposed of within two weeks from the date of receipt of the records.

3. After the order of remand was made by the High Court the application for stay of execution proceeding was reheard and that was also rejected by order dated 1-11-87. The plaintiff opposite parties again moved this Court in Civil Revision No. 8 of 1988 which was renumbered as Civil Revision No. 1038 of 1990 which was heard on 23-1-91 and 24-1-91 and this court again made the Rule absolute on 4-2-91 and further proceedings of Title Execution Case of the Assistant Judge. Sadar Sylhet was stayed for a period of four months. A direction was made by this court to dispose of the suit within that period.

4. It is alleged that the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 114 of 1990 had not taken any steps in the suit long after the expiry of four months. The suit was ultimately fixed on 5-8-1991 for taking steps with regard to the service of summons upon the defendant No. 55 and for not taking steps the suit was dismissed for default on the said date.

5. Thereafter the opposite parties being the petitioner filed an application on 5-3-92 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for restoration of Title Suit No. 114 of 1990 after setting aside the order of dismissal dated 5-8-91. In the said application it was stated by the plaintiffs opposite parties that after the case was transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge Sadar, Sylhet, they were not aware of the date as to the proceeding of the suit and that due to the serious illness the plaintiff could not attend the court nor could they contact the lawyer to know the date from their lawyer. The plaintiffs also prayed for condonation of delay in filing the application under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the self same ground.

6. The learned Senior Assistant Judge after hearing the parties allowed the application under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereby restored the suit to its original file and number by order dated 28-2-93. The petitioners have challenged the legality of the said order in this revisional application.

7. Mr BK Das, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the sufficient cause by which the plaintiffs were prevented from appearing before the court was not proved by any cogent evidence and, as such, the learned Assistant Judge was not justified in allowing the application under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that already there was an order passed by this court in Civil Revision No.1038 of 1990 directing the trial Court to dispose of the suit within four months, and the plaintiffs having not taken any steps in the suit for disposal of the suit according to the said direction, are not entitled to any discretionary relief.

<u>8. Mr BK Das, the learned Advocate referred to me from the application only one date ie 5-8-91 when the suit was fixed for taking steps by the plaintiffs. No other dates were fixed and on the said date the suit was dismissed for default. In view of the provision of Order 9 rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure the court cannot dismiss the suit for not taking any steps with regard to service of summons before the expiry of three months. Order 9 rule 5 CP Code runs as follows 5(1) Where, after a summons has been issued to the defendant, or to one of several defendants, and returned unserved the plaintiff fails, for a period of three months from the date of the return made to the Court by the officer ordinarily certifying to the Court returns made by the serving officers, to apply for the issue of a fresh summons the Court shall make an order that the suit be dismissed as against such defendant, unless the plaintiff has within the said period satisfied the court that—</u>

<u>(a) he has failed after using his best endeavours to discover the residence of the defendant who has not been served,</u>

<u>(b) such defendant is avoiding service or process, or</u>

<u>(c) there is any other sufficient cause for extending the time, in which case the Court may extend the time for making such application for such period as it thinks fit.</u>

<u>(2) In such case the plaintiff may (subject to the law of limitation) bring a fresh suit."</u>

<u>9. But in the instant case only one date was fixed for taking steps and the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit for default for not taking step. In that view of the matter the order dated 5-8-91 suffers from legal infirmity.</u>

10. It is an admitted fact that the suit was transferred to the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sylhet and the parties were not informed by any notice or otherwise and the cases of the plaintiffs opposite parties is that they could not know the date after the suit was transferred to that court. In such circumstances it was the duty of the transferee court to inform the parties about the date fixed. However the learned Assistant Judge having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record was satisfied that the plaintiffs were not at fault and thereby restored the suit to its number and file. By the said order the learned Assistant Judge has not committed any illegality which could be interfered with by this court.

11. In view of the earlier direction made by this court for disposal of the suit within four months, the plaintiffs are directed to take necessary steps in the suit to make the suit ready for hearing, without any default.

In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs, send down the lower court records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated July 3, 1997 passed by the High Court Division, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.4118 of 1991)
full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ: The argument advanced by the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners in support of this petition is more quizzical than legal.

2. In a suit for eviction of the defendants from the suit premises, SCC Suit No.1 bf 1983 of the Second Court of Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Serajgonj, a decree was passed not at the first instance but upon review under Order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In revision before the High Court Division against the said decree the defendants raised the only question that a review does not lie in a proceeding under the Small Cause Courts Act, 1887. A Single Judge of the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 3rd July, 1997, upon a comprehensive review of the legal position clearly found that the Small Cause Courts have jurisdiction to entertain and decide a review application. It was held:

From a reading of the provisions of the Act and the Code it can be said that the Small Cause Court is invested with the jurisdiction to entertain an application for review as contemplated under section 114 read with Order 47, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It would, therefore, follow that the review application filed by the landlord in the Small Cause Court is competent and maintainable. The view taken by me gets support from the decision reported in 5 ILR Cal 699.

3. Mr Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioners, does not dispute the correctness of the decision but submits, as he did before the High Court Division also, that a review lies only from a decision on reference from a Court of Small Causes. The High Court Division rejected the submission by observing that the same was absolutely misconceived and devoid of any substance. If the learned Judge had written only one sentence in support of his view then Mr Fazlul Karim would have had no answer nor the stomach to move this petition. So it falls upon us to supply that sentence,

<u>4. Mr Karim has made the submission with reference to clause (c) of section 114 of the Code of Civil Procedure the purport of which is that a review would lie from "a decision on a reference from a Court of Small Causes". Now section 113 CPC provides that any Court may refer a case for the opinion of the High Court Division and the High Court Division may make such order thereon as it thinks fit. So, what clause (c) of section 114 provides is that, if there is a decision on a reference from a Court of Small Causes, obviously it will be a decision of the High Court Division, a review would lie or the said decision. Review from a decree or order of a Court of Small Causes will be maintainable not under clause (c) but under clauses (a) and (b) of section 114 read with Order 47 rule 1 CPC.</u>

5. The High Court Division has rightly held that the submission was absolutely misconceived.

The petition is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of judgment and decree dated 28-4-1999 passed the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 413 of 1992, reversing those dated 31-8-92 passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 24 of 1992 dismissing the suit.

2. Opposite parties as plaintiff, filed Title Suit No. 428 of 1988 before the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka against the petitioners for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land. The said suit subsequently was renumbered as Title suit No. 24 of 1992 after being transferred to the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka.

3. Short facts of the case, are that the suit land is the land of Mirpur Housing Estate under the Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development, Dhaka. The defendant No. 3 invited application for allotment of plots. On the basis of the application filed by the plaintiffs, the suit plot was allotted to them on 31-10-78 and the possession was handed over to them on 13-1-80 and the deed of the settlement was registered on 5-7-86 and the plaintiffs deposited Taka 47,251 as salami and a lease was executed and registered in their favour. The plaintiffs filed a combined plan for four-storied building and the Executive Engineer issued no objection certificate on behalf of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and the Rajuk issued letter of permission. On 25-5-88, the plaintiffs mutated their names and paid rent and got rent receipts and plaintiff No. 1 supervised the property .as attorney for all others. During the Holiday of Eid-ul-Fitr, the plaintiffs guard went to the village home. On 25-4-88, the plaintiff No. 1 went to the said plot and found unknown trespasser having a but and signboard in the name of the plaintiff No. 1 and he then requested them to evict the land and removed the structure constructed thereon but they refused and accordingly plaintiff No. 1 was compelled to lodged a GD on 25-5-88 before the police station but since the defendant No. 1 was an army person, the police did not take any steps against the illegal trespasser and then he filed the suit. Thereafter by way of amendment, the plaintiff further stated that the original allottee, one Tozammel Hossain surrendered the suit plot by way of registered deed dated 14-9-75 and got a plot in lieu of a plot in Mohammadpur Housing Society. The defendant No. 1 and 1(ka) did not acquire any right in the suit property by bainapatra or registered deed dated 1-6-88 and accordingly further prayed for declaration that the sale deed dated 1-6-88 by Tozammel Hossain in favour of defendant No. 1 is illegal, void and the defendant No. 1 and 1 (ka) are illegal trespassers in respect of the suit land.

4. The present petitioner as defendant No. 1 and 1 (ka) contested the suit by filing written statement, denying the plaint case, alleging, inter alia that Tozammel Hossain son of late Ahmed Hossain got the allotment of the suit land on 16-8-68 and as per terms and conditions of allotment, Tozammel Hossain paid first installment on 31-6-68 and after fulfilling the condition of the said allotment, the erstwhile government of East Pakistan executed and registered deed on 8-11-68 and delivered possession thereof to him, who erecting temporary residence thereon, possessed the suit land and thereafter entered in to an agreement for sale on 10-2-73 with defendant No. 1(ka), on receiving Taka 40,000 out of total consideration money of Taka 50,000 from her. Thereafter Tozammel Hossain paid remaining 2nd, 3rd, and 4th installments on 9-5-88 to the defendant No. 3. The surveyor of the said office issued a letter on 23-5-88 regarding the satisfaction of the full payment of the salami and a lay out plan of the suit plot was approved by Rajuk on 11-7-88, after being recommended by the concerned housing officer. After obtaining per-mission from the concerned office, Tozammel Hossain executed and registered a deed of sale in favour of defendant No. 1(ka), who is in possession after mutating her name, paying rents to the municipality as well as paying gas bill, electric bill, water bill on his name and the government has no right to lease out the self-same property twice in favour of the plaintiff and the plaintiff's claim is false and the suit is thus liable to be dismissed with cost.

5. By the judgment and decree dated 31-8-92, the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit on contest. Being aggrieved there against, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 413 of 1992 before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka, which was heard on transfer by the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, who by the impugned Judgment and decree allowed the appeal and on reversing the judgment of the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs.

6. Being aggrieved there against the defendants obtained the instant Rule.

7. Mr TH Khan along with Mr. Sk. Hassan Arif, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner on referring to the judgment of the Courts below submits that the learned Assistant judge after elaborate discussion of the evidences on record clearly found that the story of surrender as put forward by the plaintiff was not being successfully proved in Court by the plaintiff and that the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 did not have any authority to lease out the suit land in favour of the plaintiff twice for self same land and thus dismissed the suit rightly but the appellate Court without at all reversing the said material findings of the trial Court allowed the appeal arbitrarily and accordingly it was not a proper judgment of reversal under Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that there may be thousands of defects in the defendants case but for the same, the plaintiffs will not get a decree, he is required to prove his own independent case. In the instant case the plaintiff contended that the original allottee Tozammel Hossain surrendered the suit land in favour of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 in lieu of a plot in the Mohammadpur Housing Society. Under section 68 of the Evidence Act, the plaintiff is required to prove the validity as well as legality of the story of surrender but the plaintiff has totally failed to prove the story of surrender by adducing sufficient material witnesses. He then further submits that at present, there is no provision for surrender in any law. Lastly on showing the deposition of one Nuruzzaman deposing in Court on behalf of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 supporting the plaintiffs case and stated that "document of surrender is lying with the record in their office" but the said document was not been brought before the Court in order to prove the plaintiffs contention, thus in view of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act the defendant will get the benefit about the presumption that if the document is placed before the Court, it will speak, otherwise not supporting the plaintiffs case and, as such, it was not been placed before the Court. Considering this aspect of the case, the learned Assistant judge has correctly found that the alleged story of surrender as claimed by the plaintiff was not been proved but the appellate Court has failed to consider that aspect of the case and accordingly the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.

8. Mr. Minhazul Haque, the learned Advocate along with Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, appearing on behalf of the opposite parties in reply, submits that the plaintiff is neither a recipient nor a executants of the deed of surrender, accordingly save and except the certified copy of the deed in question, he obtained nothing, which has rightly been placed and the plaintiff took all measures to prove the said document by obtaining an order from the Court for calling the original document from the custody of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 as well as to bring the volume of the deed but subsequently it was not been complied with by the defendants and, as such, the Court below on taking into consideration of the certified copy of the said deed of surrender under section 65 of the Evidence Act, together with the document which were exhibited in Court and marked as Exhibits 7-8, wherein it appears that the first installment of the deed of lease has been adjusted with the subsequent lease deed dated 6-12-75 in favour of Tozammel Hossain, given a plot in Mohammadpur Housing Estate, found the existence of the deed of surrender dated 14-9-75. If these two sets of document are taken up together, the factual aspect of the case to the effect that suit land was surrendered in favour of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 in lieu of a plot of Mohammadpur Housing Estate, found to be true. The learned Subordinate Judge has correctly considered that aspect of the case and rightly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. There is nothing wrong in the said judgment and thus this Rule is liable to be dismissed.

9. Heard the learned Advocate of both the sides and perused the impugned judgment and the lower Courts record.

10. In the instant suit, admittedly the suit land was belonged to the government and was allotted to one Tozammel Hossain by way of a registered deed dated 8-11-68. The plaintiff contended that the said Tozammel Hossain subsequently surrendered the said plot in favour of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 in lieu of a better plot in the Mohammadpur Housing Estate by way of a registered deed dated 14-9-75 and thereafter the suit land was again leased out in favour of plaintiff on 31-10-78. But as per the defendants contention, the suit plot was admittedly leased out to Tozammel Hossain by way of registered deed dated 8-11-68 and possession was handed over to him. While he was in possession, he sold the same in favour of defendant No. 1(ka) by registered sale deed dated 1-6-88 and since then she is in possession therein. In view of the case and counter case, the question to be decided here whether Tozammel Hossain at all surrendered the suit plot in favour of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 or he remained in possession thereon till it was sold in favour of the defendant No. 1 (Ka) vide registered sale deed dated 1-6-88. 11. Before considering the plaintiff's contention of surrender, I like to consider the defendant's case first.

12. In the written statement defendant No. 1 has clearly stated that –

“১৭(ছ) ইতিমধ্যে বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির মূল মালিক জনাব তোজাম্মেল হোসেন তাহার প্লটের ২য়, ৩য় ও ৪র্থ কিস্তিৱ বাকি অর্থ ৯-৫-১৯৮৮ইং তারিখে শ/৪৬ নং চালানের মাধ্যমে ট্রেজারীতে জমা দেন এবং একই তারিখে উক্ত ট্রেজারী চালান কমিশনার, সেটেলমেন্ট, পূর্ত মন্ত্রণালয় এবং নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী গৃহ সংস্থান বিভাগ-১ জমা দেন ৷

অতঃপর গৃহ সংস্থান বিভাগ-১ কর্তৃক জনাব তোজাম্মেল হোসেনের বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির দখল ও সম্পূর্ন টাকা পরিশোধিত হইয়াছে বলিয়া ২৩-৫-৮৮ ইং তারিখে সার্ভেয়ার দ্বারা একটি তদন্ত বিবরনী পেশ করেন ৷

(জ) উক্ত তোজাম্মেল হোসেনের নামে বিরোধীয় প্নটের একটি লে-আউট প্ল্যান ঢাকা গৃহ সংস্থান বিভাগ-১ এর নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী অনুমোদন করেন এবং ডি,আই,টি,বর্তমান রাজউক কর্তৃক উক্ত লে-আউট প্ল্যানটি ১১-৭-৮৮ ইং তারিখে রাজউক/৩ সি/ই ১৮৪/w/ ৪১৯২ নং স্বারকে অনুমোদন প্রদান করেন ।

(ঝ) বরাদ্দ প্রাপ্তির শর্ত সমূহ পালন করিয়া এবং ত্রান ও পুনর্বাসন গনপূর্ত সংস্থা হইতে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হস্তান্তরের অনুমতি গ্রহন করিয়া মূল মালিক জনাব তোজাম্মেল হোসেন চুক্তি মোতাবেক অত্র জবাব দানকারী জনাব এ, কে, এম, হাসানুজ্জামান এর স্ত্রী মিসেস নিগার সুলতানা আক্তারকে তাহার সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের সাফ কবলা দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়া লওয়ার অনুরোধ করেন ৷ অত:পর উক্ত সম্পত্তি ক্রয় বিক্রয়ের বা হস্তান্তরের জন্য উপ কমিশনারের ছাড়পত্র গ্রহণ করেন, গেইন ট্যাক্স প্রদান ও তল্লাশি ফি জমা দেওয়ার রশিদ গ্রহণ করে মিরপুর সাব রেজিস্টারি অফিসে ০১-৬-৮৮ ইং তারিখে জনাব তোজাম্মেল হোসেন বক্রী মূল্য গ্রহন করিয়া নালিশী সম্পত্তি অত্র জবাব দানকারী এ ,কে,এম, হাসানুজ্জামানের স্ত্রী মিসেস নিগার সুলতানা আক্তারের বরাবরে সাব কবলা দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়া দেন ৷ ”

Which means Tozammel Hossain while remaining in possession paid 2nd and 3rd installments after obtaining permission from the concerned office to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the defendant No. (ka).

13. Now let us see how this contention has proved by the DWs in Court.

14. DW No. 1 while deposing in Court replied on the cross examination made by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff that-

আমার দাখিলি জবাবের বা অনুচ্ছেদের উল্লিখিত হস্তান্তরের অনুমতি পত্র আদালতে দাখিল করি নাই। কোন অনুমতি হাউজিং থেকে নেওয়া হয় নাই বটে ৷

15. Now let us examine the lease deed' dated 8-11-68, given in favour of Tozammel Hossain, which was exhibited in Court as Exhibit 1 (ka). In clause 19 in the said deed runs as follows:—

"19. That the Tenant shall not sell, charge, mortgage, exchange, gift away or otherwise assign, sublet, encumber or in any way part with or dispose of the demised property or any part thereof before the construction of the buildings, outhouses and appurtenances hereby covenanted to be erected, except with the permission of Government."

16. In view of the above provision of the lease deed, the lease is debarred from transferring the suit property in any way before the construction of the building, except with the permission of the government. But in the instant case, as I have stated above that the defendant No. 1 has admitted in his deposition that no permission was obtained prior to the sale dated 1-6-88 in favour of his wife. As per the payment of salami, defendant has stated as I have quoted above from the written statement that he paid entire 2nd, 3rd and 4th installments of Tk. 6,398 on 9-5-88, long after the agreement for lease dated 8-4-68 in favour of Tozammel Hossain. Now again I like to consider the schedule 2 of that lease deed (Exhibit. 1 (Ka)), where it has been stipulated that how the salami is to be paid by installment, which runs as follows:—

"Schedule-II

1. The Tenant has paid premium of Rs. 2,917...(Rupees Two thousand nine hundred seventeen only  ) on allotment and the Balance of Rs. 6,389 (Rupees Six thousand three hundred eighty nine only  ) shall be paid as follows:-

(a) Rs. 2,188 (Rupees Two thousand one hundred eighty eight only ...) in the 2nd year; Rs. 2,188 (Rupees Two thousand one hundred eighty eight only...) in the 3rd year; Rs. 2,013  (Rupees Two thousand thirteen only ) in the 4th year."

17. The payment of the balance herein mentioned payable in the years herein indicated shall be paid on the anniversary of the date of first part payment of premium referred to in the second recital of this Indenture or on the first working day next following.

In clause 4 of the schedule II it has been stipulated that—

"in case of default in paying any installment or installments of salami the Tenant shall pay interest at the rate of 61/4 per cent per annum until full realisation without prejudice to the right of re-entry or other rights of the Lessor hereinbefore reserved."

18. Thus from the said schedule it appears that although the allottee said Tozammel Hossain has paid the first installment of salami, but the balance of Taka 6,389 was due from him which was supposed to be deposited by three consecutive years. In case of any default in paying the installments, he is required to pay an interest at the rate of 61/4 percent, per annum and from the written statement, I have observed above that the allottee alleged to have deposited the entire 2nd, 3rd and 4th installment of total Taka 6389 on 9-5-88 and a document showing of depositing the same has been exhibited by the defendant in Court, which was marked as Exhibit Ga (1). But from the said document surprisingly I have noted that it was shown to have been deposited only Taka 6,389 but without any interest, although it has alleged to be paid long after 20 years of the granting lease on 8-4-68 in favour of the Tozammel Hossain. Thus from the plain reading of that document, doubt may cast about the genuinely of that document as well as payment of installment by the allottee Tozammel Hossain and accordingly the document, exhibited in Court as Exhibit 1 (Uno) showing the admission of possession by Tozammel Hossain in to the suit land on making full payment of salami as asserted by one surveyor of the Metropolitan Housing Sub-division 2, Dhaka Housing Division-1, Section-2, Mirpur, Dhaka on a plain paper is also cannot be relied upon.

19. Considering the above all aspects of the defendants case, it can be held that the defendant's story to the effect that the allottee Tozammel Hossain after paying one installment, transferred the suit land in favour of the defendant legally, with full satisfaction of the requirement of the law does not stand on legal footing.

20. Now it is settled principle of law that there may be a thousands of defect in the defendants case but for the same plaintiff will not get a decree of his title, unless and until he has successfully able to prove his own independent case.

<u>21. The plaintiff contended that the said Tozammel Hossain after obtaining lease, surrendered the suit land in favour of the government by way of registered deed of surrender dated 14-9-1975 in lieu of a better plot in Mohammadpur Housing Society and thereafter the plaintiff obtained the lease of the said land. Now let us see, how the plaintiff has able to prove his case. A certified copy of the deed of surrender dated 14-9-1975 has been exhibited in Court by the plaintiff which was marked as Exhibit 7. The plaintiff also exhibited another document of lease granted in favour of Tozammel Hossain for a land to the Mohammadpur Housing Estate, which was marked as Exhibit 8. In the said deed of surrender (Exhibit 7) it was stipulated that</u>

<u>“ নিম্ন তফছিল  বর্ণিত জমি সমাপিতের দ্বারা লিজ দেওয়া হইয়াছে । যাহার বাবদ সম্পূর্ণ কারী এক কিস্তিতে ৷ মোট ২,৯১৭ টাকা সালামী স্বরুপ সাবেক স্টেট ব্যাংকে চালান নং- সি/৭ তারিখ ৩১-৮-৬৮ইং তারিখে জমা দিয়াছি, এবং যেহ���তু ব্যক্তিগত অসুবিধার জন্য এবং সম্পূর্নকারী কে মোহাম্মদপুরে অন্য একটি প্লট দেওয়ার আশ্বাস দেওয়ায় ৷ নিম্ন তপসিল বর্নিত জমি দায় শুন্যভাবে সমাপীতের নিকট সম্পর্ন করা গেল ৷ পরের পাতায় ২ (২য় পাতায়) উল্লিখিত প্লটের দখল নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলীর নিকট বুঝাইয়া দেওয়া হইল ৷ যাহা পত্র নং- ১১৫৩/৩ উবিশি তাং ১-৯-৭৫ স্বীকৃত হইয়াছে  উপরোল্লিখিত জমাকৃত টাকা আশ্বাসকৃত প্লটের সালামী বাবদ সম্মলিত হইবে ৷”</u>

<u>And the lease deed in favour of Tozammel Hossain dated 6-12-1975 for the plot of Mohammadpur Housing Estate (Exhibit 8), also speaks to be adjusted the said payment of first installment dated 31-8-1968. If these two documents are taken up together, the plaintiff's contention regarding the surrender appears to be correct and got reliance. From the record it further appears that on the prayer of the plaintiff, the Court passed an order directing the defendant Nos. 2-3 to bring the record, in order to prove the genuinety of the deed of surrender but subsequently there was a report from the office of the Ministry of Public Works that the said deed of surrender could not be found in the record room and accordingly the Court has to decide the matter in the absence of the original document of the same. In this context, I am of the view that in the submission made by the learned Advocate for the opposite party has got substance. Since the plaintiff has tried his level best to prove the contention about the deed of surrender but only on the ground that the original document of the said deed of surrender was not placed before the Court, his case cannot be thrown out, when Exhibits 7 and 8 apparently proved the plaintiffs contention of surrender to be true. There is no dispute about the deed of lease in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has also successfully able to prove his lease and the fact of possession and dispossession by adducing evidence and the appellate Court has discussed the same and rightly found in favour of the plaintiff. Thus when from the record it appears that the plaintiff has successfully able to prove that after obtaining the allotment Tozammel Hossain has surrendered the suit land in favour of the government and it was subsequently leased out in favour of the father of the plaintiff who thereafter remained in possession till he was dispossessed therefrom, I am of the view that the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree as prayed for and the lower appellate Court being the last Court of fact has committed no illegality in decreeing the suit. I found there are no merits in this Rule.</u>

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court is hereby affirmed and the suit is decreed.

Send down the LC Records at once.

End.
