full_judgment:
The Rule was issued at the instance of the plaintiffs on the following terms:

"Let the records be called for and issue a Rule calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-5 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree complained in the petition should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

2. The relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that the plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 246 of 1987 in the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Gaibanda praying for decree for partition to the extent of 2.11 acres of land appertaining to the jote of CS Khatian No. 79, 157 and 311 of Mouza Paschim Komarnai; jote of CS Khatian No. 407 of Mouza Purba Komarnai and to the jote CS Khatian Mouza Purba Komarnai stating inter alia that the schedule 'Ka' and 'Kha'  land to the plaint comprising the jote of CS Khatian No.79, 157 and 311 of Mouza Paschim Komarnai and CS Khatian No. 407 of Purba Komarnai and belonged to Mobarakulla in 4 annas share who used to possess the suit land in ejmali along with the other co-shares and the jote of CA Khatian No.79 and 311 of Mouza Paschim Komarnai belonged to Mobarakulla and Abarakullah in 2 annas share. Abarakullah there after, transferred his entire share from schedule 'Ga' and 'Gha' and to the plaintiffs in favour of Mobarakulla who used to possess the land in ejmali with the other co-sharers of the jote. Mobarakulla in all got an area of 2.93 acres of land from 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule and an area of 1.22½ acres of land from schedule 'Ga' and 'Gha', in all total 4.15½ acres land. While in possession Mobarakulla died leaving 3 sons Jamat, Jinat and Anayet and a daughter Khuki Mai, accordingly, each son got 1.18½ acres of land. Jamat thereafter, transferred and his entire share by kabala dated 10-3-1949 in favour of Jinat and thus Jinat got in the schedule 'Ka' and 'Ga' land to the extent of 2.37 acres of land. Jinat thereafter, died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs and that plaintiffs sold 0.37 acres of land and also purchased by kabala dated 2-5-1960 an area of 10 decimals of land and in this way the plaintiffs are in ejmali possession of 2.11 acres of land. The Other Co-shares Supjan, Rupjan, Kulupjan and Gendali sold their shares in favour of defendant No.19-22. The plaintiffs got their shares muted in the Government Sharasta and paid rent to the Government. The predecessor of defendant Nos.1-3 namely Anayetulla sold 0.70 acres of land in favour of different persons and the plaintiffs being in possession demanded partition to the co-shares on 15th Baishak, 1394 BS

but the defendant refused. The plaintiffs further stated by amendment of the plaint that the

original deed executed and registered dated 10-3-1949 by Jamat in favour of Jinat.

3. The defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 5 contested the suit by filing written statement and they admitted the entire genealogy given in the plaint but denied the existence of kabala dated 10-3-1949 allegedly to have executed by Jamat in favour of Jinat and stated inter alia that Jamat had very good relationship with Anayet who is also brother Jamat, did not transfer any land in favour of Jinat by the aforesaid kabala as alleged by the plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs by fraudulent means have created the said deed and that Jamat used to take money from Anayet often, who used to look after the properties of Jamat. Jamat wanted to gift his entire shares in favour brother Anayet but suddenly he fell ill and could not execute and register the deed in favour of Anayet. During his lifetime Jamat made an oral gift of his entire land in favour of Anayet and Anayet started to possess his own share along with the share of Jamat which had got by oral gift. After the death of Anayet, the defendants have been possessing those lands and their shares in the jotes, thereby, the share stood up to the extent of 2.57 acres of land and the defendants claimed Saham for the said area.

4. The learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit in part holding that Jamat did not transfer his entire share in favour of Jinat by kabala dated 10-3-1949 holding that the plaintiffs have not sought any remedy against the RS record which appears to have been recorded in the' name of Jamat and passed the judgment and decree dated 31-7-1991.

5. Thereafter, the plaintiffs being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred Title Appeal No. 197 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Gaibanda and eventually the appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge (Joint District Judge) who affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. It may be mentioned that the defendants did not prefer appeal against the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

6. The plaintiffs being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 15-6-1994 and 22-7-1994 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge, Gaibanda in other appeal No. 197 of 1991 affirming those of judgment and decree dated 24-7-1991 and 31-7-1991 passed of the Additional Assistant Judge Gaibanda in Other Suit No. 246 of 1987, preferred this revisional application before this Court and having heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners this Court had issued the Rule as aforesaid

7. Mr Golam Rabbani, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has placed, the judgments, of both the Courts and also taken me through the plaint, written statement and evidence of the parties and submitted that the Appellate Court has not discussed and consider the evidence as contemplated under Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and has committed error of law in passing the impugned Judgment and decree resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. The learned Advocate submitted further that in a suit for a partition the presumption of RS Khatian is immaterial inasmuch as Khatian cannot give title to the parties but the Courts below failed to consider the registered deed which is of more than 30 years and has not challenged its validity by anybody and on the face of such evidence, the findings and the decisions of the Courts below are not based on proper appreciation of evidence and law and, as such, committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate submitted that the Appellate Court failed to consider that the registered kabala dated 10-3-1949 executed by Jamat in favour Of Jinat has not been set aside by any competent Court of law and the plaintiffs having proved the existence of the document by filling certified copy as contemplated under section 65 of the Evidence Act and calling the volume from the concerned sub-registrar office and should have presumed that the document is a valid document as contemplated under section 114(E) of the Evidence Act and failing to hold that the registered deed dated 10-3-1949 has got presumptive value and in not holding, as such, the courts below committed error of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that the registered deed dated 10-3-1949 has got evidentiary value and the same is binding upon the defendants as they did not challenge the deed in any forum and, as such, both the Courts committed error of law in not giving decree on the basis of the said registered deed of more than 30 years old. The learned Advocate submitted further that the plaintiffs proved the genuineness of the deed dated 10-3-1949 calling for the volume and upon perusal of the Volume which was issued from the sub-registrar office and PW 4 proved the volume the Exhibit 3 and certified copy of the deed was marked as Exhibit 3 (Ka) by the Assistant Judge and thereby, judgments of both the Courts are not based on evidence on record and as such, are liable to be set aside as those Judgments have caused failure of Justice. The learned Advocate further submitted that the defendants could not produce any document to contradict the genuineness of the volume, the Exhibit 3 and 3(ka) and also did not prefer appeal against the judgment of the trial Court but the appellate Court failed to notice such genuine aspect of the case and passing the impugned judgment has committed error of law which is an decision in the occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate has submitted further, when secondary evidence in respect of the registered document produced and when no objection raised by the defendants or the learned Trial Judge rather the learned Assistant Judge marked the certified copy of the deed as Exhibit 3 and in view of such materials on record the Courts should have placed reliance on the evidence of PW 4 along with Exhibit 3(ka), the certified copy of the deed dated 10-3-1949 and should have decreed the suit.

8. The learned Advocate in support his contention has referred to a decision in the case of Jawala Singh vs Teja Singh reported in AIR 1924 Lahore 273 wherein it was held:

"The learned District Judge holding that although no objection had been taken this copy the plaintiff should have fulfilled the necessary condition laid down in the Evidence Act and should have secured the production of the original, disallowed the secondary evidence altogether and held that this first mortgage was wholly unproved. It has been laid down in Akbur Ali vs Bhyea Lal jha (1) Kishori Lal Goswami vs Rakhal Das Banerjee (2) and Chimanaji Govind vs Dinkar Dhondev (3) that when secondary evidence is produced in the first Court and no objection is taken either by the other side or by the Presiding Officer it is not open to the Court of Appeal to reject that evidence."

9. The learned Advocate referring to the section 90 of the Evidence Act submits that a document of more than 30 years old, if it is produced with Certified copy of a document of more than 30 years as secondary evidence (section 65 of the Evidence Act) before the Court along with the volume from the sub registrar office and proved by the agent of the sub-registrar (PW 4) should have presumed that it is a genuine document but both the Courts below having not attached the presumption to the document of more than 30 years old and passing the impugned judgments committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. He then refers to a decision in the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md Reazuddin Pk reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 where in, their lordships of the Appellate division held,

"10. An attempt has also been made to argue that the amalnama in question was wrongly accepted as evidence without any proof of its execution. The learned Counsel has, however, failed to satisfy us that the amalgam is not a 30 years old document and that it has not been produced from the proper custody. Once such a document more than 30 years old is produced from proper custody section 90 of the Evidence Act entitles the Court to presume that it is a genuine document. The contention thus merits no consideration."

"Section 65—Cases in which secondary evidence relating to documents may be given: Secondary evidence may be given of the existence, condition or contents of a document in the following cases:

(c) when the original has been destroyed or lost, or when the party offering evidence of its contents cannot, for any other reason not arising from his own default or neglect, produce it in reasonable time;

(f) when the original is a document of which a certified copy is permitted by this  Act, or by any other law in force to be given in evidence;

In case (e) or (f), a certified copy of the document, but no other kind of secondary evidence, is admissible."

"Section 90—Presumption as to documents thirty years old : Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the Court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, and it was duly executed and attested by the persons by whom it purports to be executed and attested."

Explanation—Documents are said to be in proper custody if they are in the place in which, and under the care of the person with whom, they would naturally be; but no custody in improper if it is proved to have had a legitimate origin, or if the circumstances of the particular case are such as to render such an origin probable."

10. The learned Advocate referring to the "Book:-Interpretation of Documents" page 314-315 by Mr Mahmudul Islam submitted that a document has to be interpreted as a whole and the "word" creating uncertainty in a document may be ignored where two interpretations are possible and that interpretation is to be accepted which may give meaning and effect to all parts of the document.

"Intention may prevail over the words used in case of ambiguity or vagueness, intention of the parties must be looked into and the cardinal rule is that intention as disclosed by clear and plain words shall prevail over any supposed intention of the instrument has to be construed in accord with the intention of the parties upon a reading of the whole of the instrument, the intention cannot be defeated by too strict adherence to the actual words used. If of the two possible interpretations one is consistent with the intention of the parties and the other not, the former is to be adopted. If there is ambiguity in the language employed, the intention may be ascertained from the contents of the deed with such extrinsic evidence as may by law be permitted to be adduced to show in what manner the language of the deed was related to the existing fact. The words creating uncertainty in a document may be ignored where two interpretations are possible and that interpretation is to be accepted which may give meaning and effect to all parts of the documents."

11. The learned Advocate submitted that the Courts below have discarded the existence of the document noticing loophole regarding a particular plot having an excess '0' (zero) that is (in the volume it appears as plot No. 1000/208 and in the certified copy issued as plot No. 1000/2080) without proper appreciation of the evidence of PW 4 and the Exhibit 3 certified copy issued as per volume and 3 (ka), certified copy filed by the plaintiffs and committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice.

12. None appears on behalf of the opposite parties.

13. I have perused the judgments of both the Courts, the evidence of the parties and Exhibit 3 and 3(ka), it appears that the trial court held that Jamat have not executed the kabala deed dated 10-3-1949 in favour of the Jinat and the plaintiffs could not prove the deed and also held that Jamat did not also make oral gift in favour of his another brother Anayet holding that Jamat till his death had been possessing the suit land by himself and as a result, contesting heirs of the two brothers will inherit the property as per Muslim law. The learned Assis6nt Judge also held that the contesting parties have not made clear statement regarding the heirs of Jamat and, as such, the decree as per prayer of the plaintiffs as well as on the basis of the claim of the defendants cannot be given. The learned trial Court ultimately given decree in part in favour of the plaintiffs to the extent of 1.28½ acres of land and saham was given to the defendants to the extent of 1.28½ acres and thus preliminary decree was given against defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 5 ex parte against the rests.

14. The Appellate Court has affirmed the preliminary decree given in favour of the plaintiffs and also affirmed the saham given in favour of defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 5. The Appellate Court also affirmed the findings and decision given by the trial Court and refused to give decree on the basis of the claim of the plaintiffs advanced through kabala deed dated 10-3-1949. The Appellate Court held further that the original Kabala deed dated 10-3-1949 had produced was forged in appreciating the contentions of the defendants. The Court also found that the plaintiffs had not stated in the plaint as to loosing of the original deed but subsequently upon amendment of the plaint introduced certain statement as to the loosing of the deed and the Appellate Court also found that the plaintiffs could not prove the statement by cogent evidence though the plaintiffs were under obligation to do so and also considered the statement regarding the loosing of the deed made in the evidence by the PW 1 and held that such statement was not corroborated by any witness in order to prove that the original deed which was allegedly executed by late Jamat. The Appellate Court also came to the findings that the plaintiffs did not take any step to prove the alleged LTI of Jinat appearing in the kabala deed by thumb impression Expert. The Appellate Court also believed the evidence of PW 4 on the finding.

বাদীপক্ষ কেবলমাত্র নালিশী দলিল ভলিয়ম তলব দিয়া পি/ডাব্লিউ ৪ নজরুল ইসলামকে দিয়া প্রমাণের চেষ্টা করিয়াছেন। পি/ডাব্লিউ ৪এর জেরা হইতে দেখা যায় যে, তিনি নালিশী দলিলের জাবেদা নকলে উল্লেখিত ১০০০/২০৮০ দাগের সহিত ভলিওমে উল্লেখিত দাগের সহিত মিল নাই মর্মে সাক্ষ্য দিয়াছেন। পি/ডাব্লিউ ৪ জেরায় বলেন যে, ভলিয়মে ১০০০/২০৮ লেখা আছে।

বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতে তর্কিত রায়ের উপরোক্ত আলোচনা সহ সমুদয় আলোচনা এবং বাদী পক্ষের মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনা করিয়া সহজেই প্রতীয়মান হয়েছে, বাদীপক্ষ তাহাদের দাখিলী ১০-৩-৪৯ইং তারিখের দলিলটি যে সঠিক তাহা উপযুক্ত মৌখিক ও দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা প্রমাণ করিতে পারেন নাই।

but in arriving at such findings the Appellate Court also has not adverted to the kabala deed dated 10-3-1949 and the evidence to its true perspective and therefore, committed error of law resulting an error in the decision occasional failure of Justice.

15. I have meticulously examined Exhibit 3, certified copy issued from the volume and also Exhibit 3(ka) certified copy of the deed dated 10-3-1949 filed by the plaintiffs which was issued upon comparison of the volume. I have perused evidence of PW 4 Md Nazrul Islam who upon requisition from the Court produced the volume containing the deed dated 10-3-1949 (page 184-186) and it was marked Exhibit 3 by the Court upon perusal of the volume. The said PW 4 during cross examination stated

ভলিয়মের ১৮৬ পৃষ্ঠায় তপসীল দাগ নং-১০০০/২০৮ লেখা আছে। (ডকে ভলিয়ম দেখিয়া) জাবেদা ১০০০/২০৮০ লেখা আছে কিনা বোঝা যায় না শূণ্যটা আলাদা রহিয়াছে। সত্য যে, ভলিয়মের উল্লেখিত এই দাগের সহিত জাবেদায় ��াগের কোন মিল নাই।

"it appears from the evidence of the PW 4 that the kabala deed in question had been compared with the volume and thumb impression of Jamal the executants as appeared in the volume along with the name of the recipient of the deed. But those aspects of the case have not been challenged by the defendants. From the evidence of PW 4 further appears that PW 4 stated "বোঝা যায় না শূন্যটা আলাদা রহিয়াছে।" Tar but the certified copy as it appears contained many plots along with plot No. 1000/208 but the certified copy Exhibit 3Ka filed by the plaintiffs contained plot No.1000/2080 resulting a '0' (zero) is excess and such excess of a '0' (zero) cannot render a deed, of 10-3-1949 which is of a document of more than 30 years i.e. the deed was registered on 10-3-1949 invalid and suit was instituted on 21-5-1987.

<u>16. On perusal of the Book (interpretation of document by Mr Mahmudul Islam as quoted above) it appears that .the intention of the parties reflected, in the deed inasmuch as the executant executed the document and omission of a '0' (zero) is merely a clerical mistake which have been committed bonfire while issuing the certified copy cannot render a document of 30 years old invalid. It is on record that the deed is of 1949. Section 90 of the Evidence Act provides that if a document is brought from the proper custody, then it entitles the Court to presume that it is a puniness document and in the present case the plaintiffs produced certified copy of the deed and also called the volume from the custody of the sub-registrar and those were marked as Exhibit 3 and 3 Ka on the basis of the evidence of PW 4 who is the agent of the sub-registrar and the Courts below on the face of such evidence of record declaring the deed dated 10-3-1949 was invalid as a whole for excess '0' (zero) written in a particular plot and coming to the findings that the plaintiffs could not prove the same are wrong finding and thereby, the Courts below committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. It has already been found that the plaintiffs submitted certified copies as secondary evidence which is contemplated under section 65 of the Evidence Act and the plaintiffs having brought the volume from the custody of the sub registrar and proving the same by a competent person (PW 4), as such, it cannot be said that the plaintiffs could not prove the deed. It is also found that the exhibit-3 Ka was admitted into evidence without any objection either from the Court or from the par-ties and in view of such materials on record I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners made relying upon the decision reported in AIR 1924 Lahore, and the decision reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76.</u>

<u>17. Upon over all evaluation of the evidence in respect of the deed of 1949, I am of the view that the plaintiffs could prove the kabala deed dated 10-3-1949 but the Courts below only on surmises rejected the deed of the plaintiffs without adverting to the legal position as well as Exhibit 3 Ka and evidence of PW 4.</u>

18. On further perusal of the evidence of the plaintiffs it appears that the Courts below have not discussed the documents of the plaintiffs inasmuch as Khatian exhibit 2 and rent receipts Exhibits 2(Ka) and 2(Kha) and also the oral evidence of PW 2 and PW 3 who deposed in order to prove the possession of the plaintiffs. On examination of the aforesaid Exhibits and oral evidence of PW 2 and PW 3 I am of the view that the plaintiffs could prove their possession covering the land of the document dated 10-3-1949 but the learned Judges have not recorded any findings with reference to those exhibits and oral evidence of PW 2 and PW 3.

19. I am of the firm view that the '0' (zero) was written after the figure '208' upon bonafide mistake for which the document of 1949 cannot be held in valid as a whole. In view of my discussions, I find that the Courts below committed the error of law in not giving decree in respect of the document dated 10-3-1949 which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice.

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The judgments of the Courts below and decrees in respect of the deed dated 10-3-1949 are set aside and the plaintiffs will get decree in respect of the land containing Exhibit 3(ka) along with the preliminary decree given by the trial Court as affirmed by the Appellate Court. The defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 5 will also get their saham as given by the trial Court to the extent of the share inherited from their predecessor Anayet. The trial Court is also directed to allow the share as mentioned in the plaint of the plaintiffs and saham of the defendant No. 2, 3 and 5.

Send down the lower Court records immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order of dismissal of the writ petitioner contained in Memo No. PMD/ SMD/BA:NA:HCCSA-4404 /3533 dated 16-5-2005 (Annexure-F) issued under the signature of respondent No. 5 dismissing the writ petitioner from service on the basis of the judgment and order dated 27-10-2004 passed by the learned Special Judge, Noakhali, in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 should not be declared to be without any lawful authority and of no legal effect.

2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule Nisi are briefly stated, as follows:

The petitioner was working as Head Cashier-cum-Sub Accountant, Sonali Bank, Chandragang Branch, Laxmipur. While he was serving in the said Branch, Manager of the said Branch, AZM Nurun Nabi, lodged a first information report (FIR) with Laxmipur Police Station which was registered as Laxmipur PS Case No. 18 dated 24-12-1997 corresponding to GR Case No. 756 of 1997 under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code, alleging discrepancy in the deposited amount of some account holders of the Bank without mentioning any figure in the Bank Scroll register and for misappropriation of Taka 9,01,000. After Investigation of the Case Police submitted charge sheet against the petitioner including two other accused on 24-5-2000. Thereafter the Office of the Prime Minister by Memo No. 23,40,04.05.12.16 /99-587(3) dated 26-8-2002 decided to withdraw the name of the accused petitioner, Md Shamsur Rahman from the prosecution of the aforesaid Laxmipur PS Case No. 18 dated 24-12-1997 and directed the District Magistrate, Laxmipur to withdraw his name. The learned Public Prosecutor, Laxmipur as per direction of the Prime Minister Office filed an application on 2-10-2002 before the Special Judge, Court No. 2, Laxmipur for withdrawal of the name of the petitioner and the learned Special Judge, Court No. 2 Laxmipur by order dated 23-11-2002 passed in the Special Case No. 3 /2003 (Laxmipur) acquitted the petitioner of the charges leveled against him under sections 409/420/467/ 468/109 of Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application to the respondent No. 4 on 27-12-2003 for seeking permission to join in the service of the Bank but in vain. Subsequently the Special Case No. 3 of 2003 (Laxmipur) was transferred to the Court of Special Judge Court, Noakhali and renumbered as Special Case No. 16 of 2003 (Noakhali). The learned Special Judge, Noakhali in the Judgment and order dated 27-10-2004 clearly noted that Accused-Petitioner Md Shamsur Rahman was acquitted of the charges leveled against him by the earlier order No. 23 dated 23-11-2002 passed in the said case. So no further comment is necessary in respect of the Accused Md Shamsur Rahman but convicted two other accused. Md Abdul Mannan and Amir Hossain Khan and sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment (RI) for 10( ten) years under section 409 and suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 (two) years under section 420 of the Penal Code with a direction for running of the sentences concurrently and to pay a fine of Taka 11,41,160 by the accused, Md Abdul Mannan, in default, to suffer RI for 7 (seven) years more and to pay a fine of Taka 1,55,000 by the Accused, Md Amir Hossain Khan, in default, to suffer RI for 3(three) years more under section 409 of the Penal Code.

3. The Assistant General Manager (AGM) of the Sonali Bank, respondent Nos. 5 issued the impugned Memo No. PMD/SMD/BA:NA HCCSA-4404 /3533 dated 16-5-2005 dismissing the petitioner from service as per judgment and other dated 27-10-2004 passed by the learned Special Judge, Noakhali in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 with effect from 27-10-2004 and directed him to refund all the subsistence allowance amount received from the time of Suspension (21-11-1993) till 26-10-2004. In default such dues of the Bank will be adjusted/realised from the dues of the petitioner and if no adjusted/ realised, the same will be realised from the petitioner through Court.

4. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application before the Chairman, Sonali Bank respondent No. 2 on 7-8-2005 for canceling the order of dismissal dated 16-5-2005 and re-instate him in service. But the respondent No. 2 did not take any step in this regard. The petitioner again applied to the Director-General. Prime Minister's Office, respondent No. 3 on 11-12-2005 to strike out his name from the Artha Rin Jari Case No. 1 of 2000 filed by the Bank and also filed an application to the Managing Director. Sonali Bank-respondent No. 4 on 29-7-2007 to re-instate him in service of the Bank. But the respondents did not take any step to re-instate the petitioner. Finally the petitioner issued a Demand of Justice notice upon the respondents on 3-2-2008. But the petitioner neither received any reply nor was he reinstated in service.

5. The petitioner did not yet attain the age of superannuation and the post of the petitioner has not yet been abolished. It is further stated that the petitioner has no liability in respect of Taka 55,000 since he has been acquitted in Special Case No. 16 of 2003. Artha Rin jari Case No. 1 of 2000 is pending against the convicted persons and not against the petitioner. So, the petitioner is entitled to be re-instated in his service. The petitioner having no other equally efficacious remedy provided by law has filed the present writ petition against the order of dismissal dated 16-5-2005 and auction Sale Notice Published in the Daily Inquilab dated 27-9-2005 passed in Artha jari Case No. 1 of 2000 by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Laxmipur for Sale of the property to the petitioner. In this backdrop the petitioner filed this writ petition-er and obtained the present rule on 9-3-2008.

6. The respondent No. 5 Assistant General Manager, Sonali Bank filed Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 28-5-2008 stating that the present writ petition is not maintainable since it relates to the terms and conditions of the service of the petitioner and as such his remedy lies before the Administrative Tribunal under section 2(aa) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980. The dismissal order of the petitioner was issued by the Assistant General Manager, Personnel Management Division, Sonali Bank, Head Office, Dhaka in accordance with law and mere acquittal of the petitioner in a Criminal case is no ground for re-instatement in the service and the appropriate authority of the Bank is the sole judgment to re-instate the petitioner. The Bank authority is competent to take disciplinary action departmentally under identical charges if it discloses adequate ground for taking action against him depart-mentally. The petitioner was dismissed by the Sonali Bank authority due to his dishonesty, misappropriation and gross misconduct, which is just, and proper. Anyway, the Sonali Bank authority filed Artha Jari Case No. 1 of 2000 against the petitioner for realisation of the decretal amount of Taka 55,000 which amount was misappropriated by him and the same is pending. Considering all the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the matter, the accused-petition was departmentally dealt with resulting in his eventual dismissal from service by the impugned Memo dated 16-5-2005.

7. The respondent No. 5 also filed Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated  15-2-2010 stating that at the time of filing of the Affidavit-in-Opposition on 28-5-2008, the respondent No. 5 could not filed the certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004. The Sonali Bank authority filed an application for obtaining certified copy of the judgment on 3-4-2005 and obtained on 10-4-2005 and, on the other hand, writ petitioner filed an application on 10-10-2005 for certified copy of the judgment and obtained the same on 17-10-2005.

8. The respondent No. 5 filed another Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 27-4-2010 stating further that the certified copy of the judgment passed in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 was obtained by the Manager, Sonali Bank Chandraganj Branch, Laxmipur on 10-4-2005 and accordingly attested copy of the certified copy was forwarded to the Assistant General Manager (AGM), Regional Officer, Sonali Bank Laxmipur by letter dated 11-4-2005. Then with reference to the letter of the Regional AGM Office dated 13-9-2005, Manager, Chandragonj Branch again obtained a fresh certified copy on 17-10-2005 and sent it to the Regional AGM office, Laxmipur by its letter dated 25-10-2005. After perusal of the fresh certified copy dated 17-10-2005, it transpires that the learned Special Judge, passed the judgment deleting the name of the Accused Md Shamsur Rahman and convicting the other accused Abdul Mannan and Amir Hossain Khan and accordingly Branch Manager by letter dated 27-10-2005 forwarded the fresh certified copy to the Regional AGM Office, Laxmipur. In this respect Manager, Chandragonj Branch by letter dated 28-2-2007 informed the AGM, Regional Office Laxmipur of the same and accordingly Regional Office by its letter dated 28-2-2007, addressed to the Assistant General Manager, Personnel Management Division, Head Office Dhaka informing the certified copy issued by the Special Judge Court, Noakhali on 17-10-2005 (Annexure-X(1) to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition) will be treated as judgment passed by the Special Judge Court, Noakhali in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 and not the certified copy of the judgment issued earlier by the Court on 10-4-2005 (Annexure-X to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition).

9. In course of hearing of the Rule, it appears to us that two judgments both dated 27-10-2009 was delivered in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 by the learned Special Judge, Noakhali. One judgment was of conviction and the other was of acquittal of the petitioner. For clarification of the matter and for proper and effective disposal of the Rule an order was passed by this Court on 18-2-2010 to transmit the entire record of Special Case No. 16 of 2003. After receipt of the case record, we have carefully and meticulously examined the entire case record. Thereafter, it transpires that only one judgment dated 24-10-2007 has been pronounced. This mistake was committed due to oversight of the earlier order dated 23-11-2002 passed by the Special Court, Laxmipur in the aforesaid Special case acquitting the petitioner but the First certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 was obtained by the Bank authority issued by the Court on 10-4-2005 did not reflect the order of the Special Court passed on 23-11-2002.

10. Subsequently fresh/corrected certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 was issued by the Special Judge, Noakhali in the Special Case No. 16 of 2003 on 17-10-2005 which reads as under:

উল্লেখ্য  যে, পরবর্তীতে মহামান্য রাষ্ট্রপতির আদেশক্রমে বিগত ২৬-৮-২০০২ তারিখে প্রধানমন্ত্রীর কার্যালয়ের পত্র সংখ্যা ২৩.৪০.০৪.০৫.১২.১৬.৯৯-৫৮৭(৩)প্রত্যাহার আদেশ এর আলোকে বিগত ২৩-১১-২০০২ইং তারিখের ২৩নং আদেশ মূলে বিচারক বিশেষ আদালত-২, লক্ষীপুর, আসামী সামছুর রহমানকে তাহার বিরুদ্ধে আনীত অভিযোগ হইতে খালাসের আদেশ প্রদান করে।

উল্লেখ্য যে, আসামী সামছুর রহমানকে মহামান্য রাষ্ট্রপতির আদেশক্রমে বিগত ২৬-৮-০২ইং তারিখে প্রধান মন্ত্রীর কার্যালয়ের পত্র সংখ্যা ২৩.৪০.০৪.০৫.১২.১৬.৯৯-৫৮৭(৩) প্রত্যাহার আদেশ মূলে বিগত ২৩-১১-২০০২ইং তারিখের ২৩নং আদেশ মূলে বিচারক বিশেষ আদালত-২, লক্ষীপুর খালাসের আদেশ প্রদান করায় অত্র আসামী সামছুর রহমান সম্পর্কে আর কোন মন্তব্যের প্রয়োজন নাই।

11. Mr Md Helaluddin Mollah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner was acquitted of the charge leveled against him by the judgment dated 27-10-2004 passed by the learned Special Judge, Noakhali in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 but the Sonali Bank authority by disobeying the judgment dated 27-4-2004 issued the impugned Memo dated 16-5-2005 dismissing the petitioner from service stating that since the petitioner was convicted and sentenced under section 409 of the Penal Code for 10(ten) years RI and under section 420 of the Penal Code for 2 (two) years RI which is illegal, malafide, without lawful authority and the same should be struck down. He further submits that after acquittal from the criminal case the petitioner made repeated prayer to reinstate him but the respondents without reinstating dismissed the petitioner from service which is illegal and without any lawful authority. He finally submits that since the Artha-Rin-Jari Case No. 1 of 2000 is not filed against the petitioner, he is entitled to be re-instated in service.

12. On the other hand, Mr M Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 5 Bank firstly, submits that the petitioner filed this writ petition against the order of dismissal from service, which certainly relates to the terms and conditions of his service and, as such, his remedy if any, shall lie before the Administrative Tribunal section 2(aa) of the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980. So, the present writ petition is not maintainable.

13. In support of his submissions, he has relied on the decisions in the case of Serajul Islam vs Director General of Food reported in 42 DLR (AD) 199 and in the case of Delwar Hossain Mia vs Bangladesh, reported in 52 DLR (AD)120. He next submits that mere acquittal of the petitioner is a criminal case is no ground for re-instatement in the service of the Bank. He lastly submits that issue the Artha Rin jari Case No. 1 of 2000 is also pending for adjudication before the Artha Rin, Adalat No. 1 Laxmipur against the petitioner for realising of Taka 55,000, considering such aspect of the matter, the petitioner should not be re-instated in service of the Bank and as such the present writ petition is not be re-instated in service of the Bank and as such the present writ petition is not maintainable under article 102 of the constitution and the Rule is liable to be dismissed with cost.

14. We have heard the learned Advocates Mr Md Helaluddin Mollah and Mr M Khaled Ahmed and perused the writ petition, Affidavit-in-Opposition, Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition, Affidavit-in-Reply and relevant Annexures annexed thereto. We have also gone through the original case of Special Case No. 16 of 2003 (Noakhali).

15. At the outset, we are to determine as to whether the writ petition is maintainable or not under article 102 of the Constitution, having regard to the fact that the petitioner filed this writ petition against the order of dismissal which certainly relates to the terms and conditions of his service and admittedly Artha Rin Jari Case No. 1 of 2000 is still pending for adjudication before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Laxmipur against the petitioner for realisation of Taka 55.000.

16. As a matter of fact, the fate of the rule depends upon our answer to the question when specific and other equally efficacious remedy was available before the Administrative Tribunal, since the petitioner is an employee of the Sonali Bank, a "Statutory public authority" specified in the schedule under section 2(aa) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended by the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 and when admittedly Artha Rin Jari Case No. 1 of 2000 is still pending for adjudication before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Laxmipur for realisation of Taka 55,000 from the petitioner.

17. Admittedly the petitioner was an employee of the Sonali Bank and posted in Chandragonj Branch, Laxmipur and it is not also disputed that he was suspended from service which he was serving as Head Cashier Cum-Sub-Accountant when Laxmipur PS Case No. 18 dated 24-12-1997 was filed by the Bank authority for misappropriations of Taka 9,01,000.

18. It was not also disputed that the petitioner was acquitted of the charges leveled against him by Court's order No. 23 dated 23-11-2002 passed by the Special Judge Court No. 2 Laxmipur in Special Case No. 3 of 2003 (Laxmi-pur), subsequently transferred to the Special Judge, Noakhali and renumbered as Special Case No. 16 of 2003 (Noakhali).

19. It was also admitted that due to over-sight and bonafide mistake of the learned Special Judge two sets of certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 was issued, firstly on 10-4-2005 (Annexure-X to the Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition) and subsequently on 14-8-2005 (Annexure-E to the writ petition) and on 17-10-2005 (Annexure-X(1) to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition) by the Special Judge Court, Noakhali. In first set of certified copy of the judgment issued on 10-4-2005, the Accused writ petitioner, Shamsur Rahman was convicted along with two other accused; but latter on, on the prayer of the Bank authority and the accused writ petitioner, the learned Special Court, Noakhali issued the corrected certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004, on 14-8-2005 and 17-10-2005 respectively. In the judgement it was clearly noted by the Special Judge, Laxmipur by order No. 23 dated 23-11-2002 that he acquitted the petitioner of the charges leveled against him, but which was not mistakenly noted in the certified copy of the judgment issued by the Special Court on 10-4-2005. Such bonafide mistake was committed in the certified copy of the judgment issued on 10-4-2005 due to oversight of the learned Special Judge. After detecting such bonafide mistake and to remove such confusion the learned Special Jude Court easily rectify such bonafide mistake by drawing up an order in the order sheet of the sand Special Case No. 16 of 2003 before issuance of the impugned certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 issued on 14-8-2005 (Annexure-E to the writ petition) and on 1740-2005 (Annexure-X(1) to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition). Thus it is evident from the case record that since no formal order was drawn up in this regard in the order sheet of the said Special Case such bonafide mistake was committed due to the facts and circumstances as stated above.

20. After examination of the lower Court record it transpires that only one judgment was delivered on 27-10-2004 by the learned Special Judge. Noakhali in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 for acquittal of the accused-writ-petitioner and conviction of two other accused Md Abdul Mannan and Amir Hossain Khan.

21. It was not denied but admitted by the parties that after passing of the judgment in the Special Case No. 16 of 2003 on 27-10-2004, the petitioner was dismissed from service by impugned memo dated 16-5-2005 (Annexure-F tot he writ petition).

22. In the case of Serajul Islam vs Director General of Food reported in 42 DLR (AD) 199 referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5, where the Appellate Division has held in paragraph 4 that if the petitioner, a Government servant, can establish a case of case of 'double jeopardy' on facts he can invoke the law under which he is proceeded against which he is proceeded against which cannot be opposed to Fundamental Rights and the Tribunal is competent to enforce the statute. The matter arising from a departmental proceeding relating to the terms and conditions of service of the petitioner, the High Court Division rightly found a bar to its jurisdiction under article 102 the constitution.

23. It has been decided by our Appellate Division in Mujibur Rahman vs Bangladesh, 44 DLR (AD) 111, In paragraph 48 it has been observed as follows:

"48. Within its jurisdiction the Tribunal can strike down an order for violation for principles of natural justice as well as for infringement of fundamental rights, guaranteed by the Constitution, or of any other law, in respect of matters relating to or arising of sub-clause (a), but such tribunals can-not, like the Indian Administrative Tribunals in exercise of a more comprehensive jurisdiction under Article 323A (see SP Sampath Kumar vs Union of India, AIR 1997 SC 386 (para 16) and JB Chopra vs Union of India AIR 1987 SC 357 (Para 2), strike down any law or rule on the ground of its constitutionality. A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental right for challenging the vires of a law will seek his remedy under Article 102(1), but in all other cases he will be required to seek remedy under Article 111(2)."

24. In the decision relied on by Mr Khaled in the case of Delwar Hossain Mia vs Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home affairs reported in 52 DLR (AD) 120, it has been clearly held in unmistakable terms that:

"A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental right for challenging the vires of a law will seek his remedy under Article 102(1), but in all other cases he will be required to seek remedy under Article 117(2)."

<u>25. There is no gainsaying the fact that the impugned order of dismissal of the petitioner dated 16-5-2005 was passed on the basis of the mistaken judgment of conviction dated 27-10- 2004 passed by the learned Special Judge, Noakhali in Special Case No. 16 of 2003. Thus there is no room for doubt that the impugned order of dismissal was issued on the basis of the judgment passed on 27-10-2004. Given this Scenario, it cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that the petitioner was dismissed for any other reason other than the reason stated in the impugned order.</u>

<u>26. In the present case, it is an admitted fact that that no order of conviction against the petitioner was in existence when the Sonali Bank authority issued the order of dismissal dated 16-5-2005. In such circumstances, the High Court Division by exercising the power of judicial review under article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the constitution was competent to inquire into the correctness of the decision if it finds that all the circumstance needed for passing the order were not present it will declare the order to void.</u>

<u>27. From the foregoing discussions and having regard to the facts and circumstance of the case, it is clear that the order of dismissal is ex-facie illegal because of the fact that when the order of dismissal was issued, there existed no order of conviction of the petitioner and as such it affected the rights or interest of the petition and thus the petitioner was treated otherwise than in accordance with law in violation of the guarantee provided by Article 31 and as such the same is liable to be struck down..</u>

<u>28. Besides, one the ground of malafide, the petitioner may come up with a writ petition by-passing the statutory alternative remedy. It is well-settled that malafide goes to the root of jurisdiction and if the impugned action is malafide, the alternative remedy provided by the statute need not be availed of.</u>

29. To render an action malafide. "There must be existing definite evidence of basis and action which cannot be attributed to be otherwise bonafide: actions not otherwise bonafide, however, by themselves would not amount to be mollified unless the same is in accompaniment with some other factors which would depict a bad motive or intent on the part of the doer of the act" (Punjab vs Khanna, AIR 2001 SC 343).

<u>30. So, our considered view is that the impugned order of dismissal dated 16-5-2005 was passed malafide, illegally and on the basis of the mistaken judgment of conviction dated 27-10-2004 passed in Serial Case No. 16 of 2003 and therefore violative of the provision of article 31 of the constitution and it is declared to be without lawful authority.</u>

<u>31. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that since the petitioner was actually acquitted and no convicted in the Special Case No. 16 of 2003 but the Sonali Bank authority illegally dismissed the petitioner from service by impugned Memo dated 16-5-2005. So direction may be passed for re-instatement of the petitioner.</u>

<u>32. In consideration of the above of the matter, we are not inclined to give such direction in respect of service of the petitioner. If the petitioner, so desires, he may approach before the appropriate authority of the Sonali Bank. The Bank authority is at liberty to take decision in the matter afresh, independently in accordance with law.</u>

33. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

34. It is declared that the impugned order of dismissal of the petitioner from service contained in Memo No PMD/SMD/BA:NA: HCCSA-4404/3533 dated 16-5-2005 (Annexure-F to the writ petition) issued by the respondent No. 5 is declared to by without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

Let a copy of this judgment be transmitted to the respondent Nos.2-6 at once for information and necessary action.

End.

lawyer:
SM Harmuz Ahmed, Advocate with Israfil Hossain, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Afsar Hossain, Advocate—For the Respondent Nos. 5-16. 
Ahmed Sohel, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 3.
parties:
Abdul Kalam Patwary ------Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and others ------Respondents
full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub J: In this Rule, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the absorption of the respondent Nos. 5-16 in the post of Assistant Director of the Directorate of National Savings, under the Ministry of Finance, Internal Resources Division should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and that under what authority the respondent Nos. 5-16 were holding their post and serving in their respective posts and as to why the respondent Nos. 1-4 should not be further directed to relieve respondent Nos. 5-16 from the aforesaid post and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, in brief, are that the petitioner, a practicing Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh had filed this writ petition for safe-guarding the national interest and to prevent draining out a huge amount of public money from the national exchequer contending, inter alia, that the employments of all manpower are made by the People's Republic of Bangladesh and all payments are made from the Public (Government) Exchequer. So far service matter is concerned of the Republic, all are governed by the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment on behalf of the respondent-government.

3. It has been stated further that for the purpose of absorption of 30 (thirty) officers process were initiated by the Ministry of Establishment for the Ministry of Finance, under the Directorate of National Savings. It has been alleged that respondent No. 2, the Secretary of the Internal Resources Division of the Ministry of Finance appointed said 30 (thirty) officers without proper examining and scrutinising their past service record. Thus, has put a huge financial burden upon the government Exchequer depriving the genuine job seekers. Further, it has been contended that in spite of bringing notice to the respondent No. 3, the Chairman of Anti-Corruption Commission of the aforesaid irregular appointment it did not take appropriate measures. It has also been stated that the said 30 (thirty) officers had been serving under respondent No. 4 and that meanwhile some of the officers having attained the age of superannuation had retired with pension benefits.

4. Bringing notice to the said illegal appointment of those 30(thirty) officers a news item under the heading “ সঞ্চয় পরিদফতরের ১২ ভুয়া কর্মকর্তা এখনও বহাল” was published in the daily "Samokal" on 17-9-2009 wherefrom the petitioner first came to learn about the said appointments alleged to have made without following due process of law. The contents of the said news item was that some 30(thirty) officers were appointed under the Directorate of National Savings, “ জাতীয় সঞ্চয় পরিদপ্তর” and meanwhile some 18(eighteen) officers had been retired who were enjoying pension benefits and that 12 (twelve) officers were still in service. It has also been alleged that those officers had secured their services under the Directorate of National Savings in connivance with some corrupt officers of the Ministry of Establishment. However, though the said matter had earlier been published in different national daily newspapers including daily "Jugantor," "Dinkal," "Prothom Alo," "Daily Khabor," "Janakantha" and "Daily Sangbad" etc. (Annexure-A series) in between the period of 2007 to 2009, but yet the respondents did not take any steps to hold any inquiry to find out the actual truth.

5. It has further been allowed that pursuant to the application made by the Assistant Director of the Directorate of National Savings on illegal appointment of the those officers in contravention of the Recruitment Rules by dint of corrupt practice, the matter was taken up for enquiry so conducted by one Mr Md Habib Ullah, the Assistant Director of Directorate of National Savings. On the basis of the said inquiry report dated 29-7-1907 it had been revealed that those 30(thirty) officers of the Directorate of National Savings were appointed without any legal basis. Despite the said report no appropriate measures had been taken by the respondents. Hence, the present application has been filed for a declaration that the absorption of the respondent Nos. 1-16 in the post of Assistant Director of the Directorate of National Savings, under the Ministry of Finance, Internal Resources Division had been made without lawful authority, (in the nature of writ of certiorari) and for a direction to oust those respondents from the respective post, (in the nature of writ of mandamus) and also challenging the authority of holding their respective posts (in the nature of writ of quo-warranto.)

6. Respondent Nos. 5-16 entered appearance by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that all these 30 (thirty) officers were absorbed in different organizations of the government under different Ministries under section 5 of the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. Further, it has been stated that similar allegations against the respondents were earlier published in "Daily Millat" and the "Daily Khabor" long back on 19-10-1997. Pursuant thereto, the Bureau of Anti-Corruption held enquiry. The allegation having not been proved against the respondent Nos. 5-16 the enquiry report was ultimately kept with the record (Annexure-II, III, IV-A and IV-B Respectively).

7. It has also been contended that respondent Nos. 9-16 were duly absorbed by the Directorate of National Savings complying all the legal requirements as prescribed by the Ordinance,1985 (Annexure-V, V-A-F respectively). However, the Gazetted Officers (Department of National Savings, Ministry of Finance) Recruitment Rules, 1979 as referred by the petitioner was applicable to the direct appointees and for departmental promotees only, not for these respondents who were absorbed under the Ordinance, 1985. In this regard it has been 'emphatically contended that in the said enquiry report held in the year 1997 it had been recommended, inter-alia, for permanent appointment of respondent Nos. 5-16 in the respective posts. Accordingly, the respondent No. 2 made the service of respondent Nos. 5-16 permanent which were published in the gazette dated 26-10-1998. (Annexure-7). Further, it has been contended that the said respondents were not directly appointed in the. Directorate of National Savings but were absorbed in the respective post as per section 5 of the "The Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985". Subsequently, those respondents were issued appointment letters by the respondent No. 2 on different dates (Annexure-8 8A 8K respectively). Moreso, from the official records it is apparent that before absorption in the Directorate of National Savings, the respondent Nos. 5, 6, 7, 8, 14 and 15 had served in the Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies (BIDS) an organisation under the Ministry of Planning; that the respondent Nos. 10,11,12,13 and 16 had served under the Directorate of Jatyio Juba Sangstha under the Ministry of Youth and Sports; and that the respondent No. 9 had worked under the Bangladesh Agriculture Research Council under the Ministry of Agriculture. All those respondents were paid as per National Pay Scale commencing from basic salary of Taka 750. Moreover, according to the clarification of the Ministry of Establishment the said respondents were public servants at the time of their absorption in the Directorate of National Savings.

8. Mr Afsar Hossain along with Mr Ahmed Sohel, the learned Advocates appearing for the respondents candidly submits that the petitioner has filed the writ petition after a lapse of 25 years for a declaration that the absorption of respondents is illegal. As such, simply on that score this Rule is liable to be discharged on the ground of inordinate delay. Further, he goes to submit that this Rule is not maintainable for the service matter so far respondents are concern is not amenable under writ jurisdiction. Moreover, the petitioner has tried to bring the service matter of the said respondents in the garb of public interest litigation though has failed miserably to how whose interest in fact he is espousing in the given facts and circumstances. Moreover, no where within the four corners of this writ petition it has been disclosed that the public at large are affected by the action of the respondent Nos. 1-4 appointing respondent Nos. 5-16 in their respective posts; and as such this writ petition cannot be treated as a public interest litigation. Me further submits that the petitioner has, in fact, filed the present writ petition with an ulterior motive in order to cause unnecessary harassment to the respondent Nos. 5-16 to serve the interest of vested quarters best known to him. Moreover, the paper clip-ping as annexed with the writ petition contained news item under the leading "317 fake government employees are found" published in the Daily "Prothom Alo" dated 8-9-2008 whereas he filed the writ petition only against 12 persons i.e., the respondent Nos. 5-16, which goes to disclose malafide act and a such on that score as well this Rule must fail. He also submits that the Gazetted Officers (Department of National Savings, Ministry of Finance) Recruitment Rules, 1979 is not applicable to these respondents, for they were not appointed directly as fresh candidates. The petitioner rather made an abortive effort to confuse this Hon'ble Court placing the said Rules, 1979 for appointment of the respondents instead of the Ordinance, 1985 hence; this Rule suffers from suppression of fact. Moreover, he submits that respondent Nos. 5, 7, 14 and 15 have already been retired from their service and that the rest are on the verge of retirement within one year. Because of the pendency of his Rule filed without any legal basis whatsoever The said retired respondents arc now living in distress and hardship and that they are not receiving any pension benefit due to the pendency of the Rule in spite of serving in their respective posts for 27 (twenty seven) years hence those respondents are seriously prejudiced. Accordingly, he submits that the petitioner having failed to substantiate any of the grounds which he has agitated this Rule should be discharged with costs.

9. Mr Ahmed Sohel, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 3 adopts the submissions so have been advanced by Mr Afsar Hossain, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of respondent Nos. 5-16.

10. In the present Rule the petitioner has in fact tried to bring the issue in the fold of writ of mandamus, certiorari as well as quowarranto challenging the absorption of respondent Nos.5-16 in the post of Assistant Director of the Directorate of National Savings, under the Ministry of Finance, Internal Resources Division alleging, inter-alia that the said absorption have not been done in due compliance of law. In support of the said claim the petitioner attempts to have relied upon the inquiry report dated 29-7-1997 as contained in Annexure-B to the writ petition.

11. Annexure-B, the inquiry report dated 29-7-1997 (a photo copy not attested by the learned Advocate certified to be true) is claimed to be the inquiry report submitted by one Md Habib Ullah, the Assistant Director (Administration) with regard to the appointment of 30 (thirty) officers. On perusal of the same it appears that it is an extract of the so-called inquiry report, not signed by the officer concern. Moreso, it is an incomplete one having no head or tail reflecting on what issue the enquiry was held and what was its findings. Thus, the genuineness of the said document on the basis of which the present Rule has been issued becomes questionable. Moreover, the petitioner has also relied his claim on the report as published in the national daily newspaper namely "Jugantor", "Dinkal," "Prothom Alo," "Daily Khabor," "Janakantha" and "Daily Sangbad" etc.

12. In Laxmi Raj Shetty vs State of Tamil Nadu reported in AIR 1988 (SC) 1274 it has been categorically found at paragraph 26.

"It is now well-settled that a statement of fact contained in a newspaper is merely evidence in the absence of the maker of the statement appearing in Court and deposing to have perceived the fact reported

13. In the said case it has further been observed that—

"A newspaper report without any further proof of what had actually happened through witnesses is of no value. It is at best a second hand secondary evidence. It is well known that reporters collect information and pass it on to the editor who edits the news item and then publishes it. In this process the truth might get perverted or garbled. Such news items cannot be said to prove themselves although they may be taken into account with other evidence if the other evidence is forcible.

<u>14. In agreement with the said observations so made by the Supreme Court of India we are also of the view that a report being published in newspaper cannot go to construe and establish the allegation of absorption of the respective respondents being taken without due process of law.</u>

15. This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner combining writ of mandamus, certiorari as well as quo-warranto. In a writ of mandamus and certiorari the person aggrieved must have legal right to agitate his claim. The Appellate Division while interpreting the term "aggrieved person" observed in Kazi Mukhlesur Rahman's case reported in 26 DLR (SC) 44, as under;

"It appears to us that the question of locus standi does not involve the court's jurisdiction to hear a person but of the competency of the person to claim a hearing, so that the question is one of discretion which the Court exercises upon due consideration of the facts and circumstance of each case.

16. Further, in Bangladesh Sangbad Patra Parishad (BSP) represented by its Secretary General, Anwarul Islam vs The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by its Secretary, Ministry of Information, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 126 it has been categorically observed, inter alia—

"The Parishad was not espousing the cause of a downtrodden and deprived section of the community unable to spend money to establish its fundamental right and enforce its constitutional remedy. The indication was thus broadly given that in case of a violation of any fundamental right of the citizens affecting particularly the weak, downtrodden or deprived section of the community or that if there is a public cause involving public wrong or public injury, any member of it he public or an organisation, whether being a sufferer him-self/itself or not may become a person aggrieved if it is for the realisation of any of the objectives and purposes of the Constitution.

17. While giving liberal interpretation to the expression "any person aggrieved" the Appellate Division in Dr Mohiuddin Farooque vs Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Irrigation, Water Resources and Flood Control reported in 49 DLR (AD) 1 observed, inter alia—

"Any person other than an officious intervener or a wayfarer without any interest or concern beyond what belongs to any of the 120 million people of the country or a person with an oblique motive, having sufficient interest in the matter in dispute is qualified to be a person aggrieved and can maintain an action for judicial redress of public injury arising from breach of public duty or for violation of some provision of the Constitution or the law and seek enforcement of such public duty and observance of such constitutional or legal provision A person pleading sufficient interest may be able to cross, what is called, the threshold stage on the averments made in the writ petition but ii will always remain open for a prospective respondent to contest the said claim on facts and also to assail the bonafides or even the appropriateness in a particular case of the petitioner for seeking a relief invoking the constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution  The Court will have to decide in each case, particularly when objection is taken, not only the extent of sufficiency of interest but also the fitness of the person or invoking the discretionary jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution."

<u>18. In, other words, the competency of the person claiming hearing of the issue in question is to be considered by the Court upon due consideration of the facts and circumstance of each case.</u>

19. In the instant case the petitioner has hopelessly failed to show that he is, in fact, espousing a public cause, that his interest in the subject matter is real and not in the interest of generating some publicity for himself or to create mere public sensation, that he is acting bonafide, that he is not a busybody or an interloper, that it is in the public interest to grant him standing and that he is not acting for a collateral purpose to achieve a dubious goal, including serving a foreign interest, as has been observed by the Appellate Division in the Dr Mohiuddin Farooque's case (Supra). Accordingly, having found no substance for consideration in this Rule, it is liable to be discharged.

20. In the result, the Rule is discharged.

There will be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
By this Rule the Opposite Party Nos. 1-5 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-6-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 40 of 1993 allowing the appeal, decreeing the suit on setting aside those dated 31-10-1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1990 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the Opposite Party Nos. 1-5 as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1999 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Kotia Chittagong for a declaration that the deed of will (অর্পন নাম) executed by Obaidur Rahman the predecessor of both the plaintiffs and the defendants dated 25-3-1981 to be illegal, fraudulent, void, inoperative alleging, inter alia, that the signatures of said Obaidur Rahman was taken forcibly upon some blank stamp papers by the defendants and by using those stamp papers they created the said Osiatnama by false personification. It was their case that Obaidur Rahman did not intend to make a will and did not execute and register that deed of will.

3. That suit was contested by the defendant No. 1 by filing written statement denying the plaintiffs case contending, inter alia, that the deed in question was duly executed by Obaidur Rahman on commission and said Obaidur Rahman expressed his intention to bequest his property by way of will. It is their case that the will in question was written as per instruction given by said Obaidur Rahman.

4. Both the parties examined witnesses in support of their respective cases. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the evidence on record came to finding that the deed of will dated 25-3-81 was duly executed and registered on commission and the plaintiffs failed to prove their case and with this observation dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1992. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred other Appeal No. 4 of 1993.

5. The Appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-6-96 allowed the appeal and decreed the suit declaring deed of will dated 25-3-81 to be a void deed.

6. Being aggrieved by this judgment and decree the defendant has obtained the instant Rule.

7. Mr Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, took me to the judgment of both the Courts below and submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge upon misconception of law and fact has decreed the suit although no evidence is available on record in support of his finding. He prayed for interference against the impugned judgment and the decree.

8. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan with Mr Mujibur Rahman supported the impugned judgment and decree. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan submitted that the deed in question is void in view of the fact that the deed of will 'Nirupan Patra' shows that the same was not executed wilfully by Obaidur Rahman and the Court of appeal rightly decreed the suit.

9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties at length and have gone through the judgments of both the Courts below very carefully. I have also gone through evidence on record meticulously.

<u>10. On perusal of the evidence of PW 1 it appears that she did not claim any relief against the deed in question in her evidence. She simply stated in her chief that she suffered loss by the deed in question. She did not adduce any evidence claiming the deed in question to be created by false personification. On perusal of the deed in question it shows that the deed was executed and registered on commission. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act provides that every official work has to be presumed to have been rightly done. The deed in question having been executed and registered on commission there is no scope to say that the said deed was forged unless any positive evidence is adduced. There is no other evidence available on record to declare the deed to be a forged or void one. In view of the above, I have reason to believe that the learned Subordinate Judge being the last Court of fact committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in declaring the deed in question to be void.</u>

<u>11. On perusal of the pleadings as well as the evidence on recor, it appears that the parties to the deed in question are the heirs and legal representatives of the Late Obaidur Rahman. The deed in question having been made in favour of the co-sharers of Obaidur Rahman the plaintiff may seek remedy in a properly instituted partition suit.</u>

12. In the facts and circumstances and the discussions made above I find merit in the Rule.

13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute however without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-6-1996 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 40 of 1993 are hereby set aside. The judgment and decree dated 31-10-1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 59 of 1990 are hereby restored. The order of stay granted by this Court dated 13-8-1996 is hereby vacated.

The office is directed to send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.
